ROSWELL 1947: WHAT FELL FROM THE SKY—AND WHY THE MYSTERY REFUSES TO DIE

A rancher found strange wreckage, the United States Army announced it had captured a flying disc, and within hours the story changed. Nearly eighty years later, Roswell remains the most disputed UFO case in history.

By Rob McConnell — August 21, 2026

Something came down in the New Mexico desert during the summer of 1947.

That much is beyond serious dispute.

Debris was discovered on an isolated ranch northwest of Roswell. Military personnel from Roswell Army Air Field recovered it. The wreckage was transported through military channels, and on July 8, 1947, the Army issued an astonishing public statement announcing that it had taken possession of a “flying disc.”

Only hours later, the military withdrew that announcement and displayed the remains of what officials described as a weather balloon.

Decades afterward, retired officers and local residents began telling a much more extraordinary story: the recovery of an unusual craft, small nonhuman bodies, heavily guarded crash locations and an extensive government operation designed to conceal humanity’s first confirmed encounter with extraterrestrial life.

The United States Air Force eventually acknowledged that its original weather-balloon explanation was incomplete. It argued that the wreckage came from Project Mogul, a classified Cold War balloon program intended to detect Soviet nuclear tests.

That admission answered some questions but created others.

Why did trained intelligence personnel at the only atomic-bomb unit in the world mistake balloon debris for a flying saucer? Why did the Army announce the capture of a disc before identifying the material? Why did witnesses wait decades before mentioning bodies? Why do the alleged crash locations, dates and descriptions vary? Why are there no verified photographs, biological samples or authenticated pieces of extraterrestrial wreckage?

Roswell is not one mystery. It is several mysteries layered together: a real 1947 recovery, a genuine military reversal, Cold War secrecy, disputed testimony, questionable documents, proven fabrications and an enduring human desire to know whether we are alone.

America’s flying-saucer summer

The Roswell incident occurred during an extraordinary moment in American history.

On June 24, 1947, civilian pilot Kenneth Arnold reported seeing nine unusual objects flying near Mount Rainier in Washington State.
Arnold described their motion as resembling saucers skipping across water. Newspaper accounts transformed that description into the term “flying saucers.”

The expression spread around the world.

During the following weeks, newspapers published hundreds of reports of mysterious objects. Some were likely aircraft, balloons, astronomical objects or misperceptions. Others remained unexplained. Practical jokers threw homemade discs into fields, and an anxious public looked skyward.

This was also the beginning of the Cold War. The Soviet Union was becoming America’s principal adversary. Captured German rocket technology was being developed rapidly. Secret military aircraft and balloon programs operated over the American Southwest.

Into that atmosphere stepped rancher William Ware “Mack” Brazel.

Mack Brazel finds the debris

Brazel worked the Foster Ranch, approximately 75 miles northwest of Roswell. Accounts differ over exactly when he discovered the wreckage.

In his contemporary newspaper statement, Brazel said that he and his young son encountered the material on June 14, although he had noticed unusual debris earlier. Other later accounts placed the discovery closer to the beginning of July, possibly after a severe storm.

The wreckage was spread across an area of the ranch. Brazel described rubber strips, tinfoil-like material, tough paper and sticks. 
Contemporary reports did not quote him describing an intact spacecraft, engines, seats, instruments or bodies.

Brazel gathered some of the debris. After hearing local conversations about flying saucers, he travelled to Roswell and reported the discovery to Chaves County Sheriff George Wilcox.

Wilcox contacted Roswell Army Air Field.

That decision brought Major Jesse A. Marcel, the intelligence officer of the 509th Bombardment Group, and counterintelligence officer Sheridan Cavitt into the story. Marcel and Cavitt accompanied Brazel to the ranch and recovered material.

The significance of Marcel’s position cannot be ignored. The 509th was the world’s only operational atomic-bomb group. Its intelligence officer was not an inexperienced private unfamiliar with aircraft or military equipment.

Whatever Marcel saw, his superiors considered it important enough to report up the chain of command.

“RAAF captures flying Saucer"

Colonel William Blanchard, commander of the 509th, authorized public information officer Lieutenant Walter Haut to issue a press release.

The statement announced that the “many rumours regarding the flying disc became a reality” when the intelligence office of the 509th gained possession of a disc recovered through the cooperation of a rancher and the sheriff’s office.

The announcement was distributed to local radio stations and newspapers.

On July 8, 1947, the Roswell Daily Record published the headline that would eventually become one of the most famous in newspaper history:
“RAAF CAPTURES FLYING SAUCER ON RANCH IN ROSWELL REGION.”

The article reported that Marcel and a military detail recovered the disc and that it was flown to “higher headquarters.” It offered no description of extraterrestrial occupants or a complete spacecraft.
 
The announcement produced immediate international interest. Telephone lines were overwhelmed. Reporters descended upon military offices and attempted to reach everyone involved.

Then the story changed.

General Ramey and the weather balloon

The material was transported to the headquarters of the Eighth Air Force in Fort Worth, Texas, commanded by Brigadier General Roger Ramey.

Ramey told reporters that the recovered object was not a flying disc. It was a weather balloon and its radar reflector. Photographs showed Ramey, his chief of staff Colonel Thomas Dubose, and Marcel with pieces of foil, rubber and what appeared to be the remains of a radar target.

The sensational story disappeared almost as quickly as it had begun.

For approximately thirty years, Roswell was not the centrepiece of UFO culture it is today. It was rarely discussed, even as other flying-saucer cases gained attention.

That silence matters. Proponents argue it demonstrates the effectiveness of military intimidation and secrecy. Skeptics argue it shows that the alien-craft narrative had not yet been created.

Jesse Marcel changes the story

Roswell returned to public attention in 1978 when nuclear physicist and UFO researcher Stanton T. Friedman interviewed the retired Jesse Marcel.

Marcel said the material he handled was unlike anything he had encountered. He described thin metal that reportedly could not be burned, cut or permanently creased. Other accounts associated the wreckage with exceptionally strong, lightweight beams bearing unusual symbols.

Marcel also maintained that the material photographed in General Ramey’s office was not the important wreckage recovered from the ranch. He believed ordinary balloon debris had been substituted before reporters arrived.

Marcel did not claim to have seen alien bodies. His testimony concerned debris.

His story became a foundation of The Roswell Incident, the influential 1980 book by Charles Berlitz and William L. Moore. The book proposed that an extraterrestrial spacecraft had crashed and that the government concealed the discovery.

Once Roswell became famous, investigators located increasing numbers of witnesses. Unfortunately, the developing accounts did not always agree.

One crash site—or several?

The original 1947 story concerned scattered debris on the Foster Ranch.

Later versions introduced a second location where investigators allegedly discovered a more substantial portion of the craft and its occupants. Other witnesses placed a crashed vehicle on the Plains of San Agustin, approximately 150 miles away. Still more accounts described different sites north of Roswell.

These multiplying locations created a major difficulty.

Researchers attempted to reconcile them by proposing that a spacecraft exploded, skipped across the landscape or separated into sections, leaving a debris field in one place and the main vehicle elsewhere. That is possible as a theory, but it was not part of the documented 1947 account.

A responsible investigation must distinguish between contemporary evidence and retrospective testimony introduced decades later.

The stories of alien bodies

The most sensational portion of the Roswell legend—the recovery of extraterrestrial bodies—did not appear in the known July 1947 news coverage.

Later witnesses described small humanoid beings with large heads, enormous eyes, thin limbs and greyish skin. Some said the bodies were dead; others suggested one creature survived temporarily.

Alleged destinations for the bodies have included:
• Roswell Army Air Field 
• Fort Worth 
• Wright Field, later Wright-Patterson Air Force Base 
• Los Alamos 
• Kirtland Army Air Field 
• Other classified facilities 

No publicly authenticated military document records the recovery, transportation, examination or storage of extraterrestrial remains from Roswell.

That absence does not automatically disprove a deeply classified operation. It does, however, mean the body-recovery story rests primarily upon testimony given many years after the event.

Glenn Dennis and the missing nurse

Roswell mortician Glenn Dennis claimed that military personnel contacted his funeral home inquiring about small, hermetically sealed caskets and methods of preserving bodies. Dennis later said he encountered a frightened nurse at the air base who described participating in, or witnessing, examinations of strange bodies.

According to Dennis, the nurse was subsequently transferred and disappeared from his life.

Investigators attempted to identify her, but the names Dennis supplied did not produce a convincing match. His account changed in significant ways, and critics concluded that the nurse story was unreliable.

The claim became enormously influential because it gave the alien-body narrative a medical setting. Yet without an identified nurse, records or supporting witnesses, it remains an uncorroborated story.

Frank Kaufmann and Gerald Anderson 

Frank Kaufmann presented himself as an important military participant with knowledge of a crashed craft and bodies. For a time, some Roswell researchers regarded him as a central witness.

After Kaufmann’s death, examination of his papers reportedly revealed forged or altered documents. Major researchers who had once cited him withdrew their support.

Gerald Anderson claimed that as a child he encountered a crashed object and bodies on the Plains of San Agustin. Researchers discovered serious problems involving his chronology and supporting materials. A diary offered in connection with the account was determined to have been written with ink not manufactured until years after its alleged date.

These cases do not disprove every Roswell allegation. They demonstrate how fabricated evidence and unreliable witnesses contaminated the investigation.

Walter Haut’s later affidavit

Walter Haut was the public information officer who issued the original flying-disc announcement.

For years, Haut’s public statements were relatively restrained. After his death, an affidavit signed in 2002 was released in which he reportedly claimed to have seen a craft and bodies inside a hangar.

Supporters regard the affidavit as powerful testimony from the man at the centre of the original announcement. Critics question why such dramatic details appeared so late, whether Haut’s memory had deteriorated, how the affidavit was prepared and why his earlier public accounts were less extraordinary.

Once again, Roswell presents an evidentiary dilemma: a potentially important witness making his strongest statement more than half a century after the event, without physical evidence to accompany it.

What was Project Mogul?

In the 1990s, the United States Air Force conducted an extensive investigation into Roswell. Its principal conclusion was that the Foster Ranch debris came from Project Mogul.

Project Mogul was a highly classified program intended to detect evidence of Soviet atomic-bomb tests. The project used long trains of balloons carrying acoustic sensors and radar reflectors to high altitude.

The balloons, rubber components, foil-backed radar targets, wooden supports and adhesive tape could produce a large field of unfamiliar wreckage after crashing and remaining exposed to sunlight and weather.

One radar-target manufacturer reportedly used tape decorated with floral or geometric designs. Those patterns have been proposed as the source of later memories of strange symbols or “hieroglyphics” on pieces of the wreckage.

The Air Force identified an unrecorded or informally designated June 4, 1947 launch, commonly called Mogul Flight 4, as the probable source. Tracking was reportedly lost as the balloon array travelled in the general direction of the Foster Ranch.

The project’s purpose—not necessarily every individual balloon component—was secret. Therefore, military officials could publicly call it a weather balloon without revealing that it was part of an effort to monitor the Soviet Union.

The full Air Force investigation is available in The Roswell Report: Fact Versus Fiction in the New Mexico Desert.
 
Problems with the Mogul explanation

Project Mogul is supported by real records, real equipment and a genuine national-security purpose. It is not an invention created from nothing in the 1990s.

Nevertheless, critics identify unresolved problems.

There is no universally accepted surviving record explicitly stating that Flight 4 launched successfully and landed on the Foster Ranch. Some documentation indicates that a planned flight was cancelled because of cloud conditions, although researchers argue that a cluster of balloons was still released.

The timing is also debated. If Brazel discovered the material around June 14, why did he wait until early July to report it? If the wreckage had been spread across the ranch for weeks, why did it suddenly become urgent?

Critics further argue that weather balloons and radar targets were not so exotic that Marcel, Cavitt and other military personnel should have mistaken them for a flying disc.

Supporters of the Mogul explanation answer that Marcel was not part of the classified program, that the large balloon train was unusual, that newspaper language exaggerated the Army’s initial conclusion and that the military moved quickly to suppress publicity because Mogul’s mission was secret.

What about the bodies and test dummies?

The Air Force’s 1997 follow-up report, The Roswell Report: Case Closed, attempted to explain reports of alien bodies.

It proposed that witnesses had combined memories of several later military activities, including anthropomorphic test dummies dropped from high-altitude balloons during the 1950s, aircraft accidents and recovery operations involving injured or deceased personnel.

The test dummies were approximately human-shaped, transported on stretchers and recovered by uniformed military teams. From a distance—or in memories altered over decades—such operations might resemble the recovery of strange bodies.

The explanation has a conspicuous weakness: the dummy-drop operations began years after 1947.

The Air Force argued that memories of separate events became compressed over time. Critics understandably ask why a 1950s event should be accepted as the explanation for testimony supposedly concerning July 1947.

This does not prove alien bodies were recovered. It means the government’s explanation for every body report is less straightforward than the Mogul explanation for the ranch debris.

The missing records

New Mexico Congressman Steven Schiff asked the United States General Accounting Office—now the Government Accountability Office—to investigate government records concerning Roswell.

The GAO searched records held by multiple agencies. It found no documentation establishing the recovery of extraterrestrial material. It also found that some administrative records from Roswell Army Air Field had been destroyed.

The outgoing-message records from the base for the relevant period and certain administrative files had been disposed of without documentation clearly establishing when, how or under whose authority the destruction occurred.

That finding fuelled suspicions of a cover-up.

However, missing records are not automatically evidence that alien-recovery documents were deliberately destroyed. Government agencies routinely lost or destroyed records under inconsistent retention procedures. The GAO could not establish that the missing files contained information about a spacecraft or bodies.

The official GAO finding therefore cuts both ways: it discovered no proof of extraterrestrial recovery, but it also could not account fully for the destruction of potentially relevant records.
 
The Ramey memorandum

One of the original Fort Worth photographs shows General Ramey holding a piece of paper. Researchers have used photographic enhancement to attempt to read the document.

Some believe the text includes words resembling “victims,” “disc” and references to Fort Worth or Roswell. Others argue that the image lacks sufficient resolution and that analysts are finding expected words in an unreadable pattern.

No uncontested reconstruction of the message exists.

If the original photograph or negative permitted a reliable reading, the memorandum could become one of the most important documents in the case. At present, competing interpretations reveal more about the limits of image enhancement than about what Ramey was actually holding.

The MJ-12 documents

In the 1980s, documents surfaced describing a secret group called Majestic Twelve, allegedly created by President Harry Truman to oversee the Roswell recovery and extraterrestrial matters.

The documents appeared to provide the missing architecture of the cover-up: named scientists, military commanders and government officials managing the greatest secret in history.

To read the rest of this story, visit https://t.co/WK2784pJSy

TINUBU AND CHAGOURY: THE BILLION-DOLLAR FRIENDSHIP NIGERIA DESERVES TO HAVE EXPLAINED

Letters from Stockholm — An Investigation into Power, Patronage and the Man Behind Some of Nigeria's Biggest Contracts

By Kio Amachree

There is a legitimate question at the heart of the relationship between President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and billionaire businessman Gilbert Chagoury, and it is bigger than gossip, ethnicity or political rivalry:

Why has a businessman with Chagoury's extraordinary history become one of the most trusted and commercially successful figures around the Nigerian presidency?

The answer matters because this is not merely about friendship. It concerns billions of dollars in infrastructure, ports, highways, valuable land and the integrity of Nigerian public procurement.

My investigation found a substantial documentary trail. I will lay that out first, fact by fact, and I will be careful to separate what is proven from what is not. Then, at the end, I will tell you what I personally believe — and I will label it as belief, because a reader is entitled to know where the documents stop and where my judgement begins.

 WHO IS GILBERT CHAGOURY?

Gilbert Chagoury was born in Lagos in 1946 to Lebanese parents. Together with his brother Ronald, he built the Chagoury Group into a sprawling conglomerate operating in construction, property development, hotels, manufacturing, telecommunications, flour milling, insurance, industrial services and finance. The group lists Hitech Construction, ITB Construction, Eko Atlantic and numerous industrial companies among its interests.

That success cannot be separated from politics.

During the military dictatorship of General Sani Abacha, the Chagourys became exceptionally influential. Contemporary Washington Post reporting described Chagoury companies as beneficiaries of major government business, including crude-oil transactions, fertilizer supply and construction projects.

Then came the Swiss investigation.

 THE ABACHA MONEY: THIS PART IS NOT AN ALLEGATION

The most significant fact about Chagoury's history is established in Swiss legal records.

In 2000, Geneva proceedings found Gilbert Chagoury guilty of money laundering and supporting a criminal organisation in connection with money diverted by Sani Abacha and his associates. The Swiss record states that he was fined one million Swiss francs and undertook to return $66 million to Nigeria.

That point needs to be stated precisely. This was not somebody accusing Chagoury in a newspaper. It arose from Swiss criminal proceedings.

Chagoury has maintained that he did not know the funds were stolen, and reporting has said the conviction was later expunged. But expungement does not erase the historical fact that the proceeding occurred, nor the finding recorded by Switzerland's judicial authorities.

For Nigerians, the obvious question becomes unavoidable: why would a government supposedly committed to fighting corruption place extraordinary confidence in a man whose name appears in one of the most notorious episodes of Nigerian state plunder?

 THEN CAME THE UNITED STATES

Chagoury's difficulties did not end with Switzerland.

In 2021, the United States Department of Justice disclosed that Chagoury had entered into a deferred prosecution agreement after a federal investigation into illegal foreign campaign contributions. The DOJ said he admitted providing approximately $180,000 that was used to make contributions to American political candidates through intermediaries, despite foreign nationals being prohibited from financing U.S. elections. He paid $1.8 million to resolve the matter.

Most strikingly, the Department of Justice said prosecutors considered his "unique assistance to the U.S. government" when resolving the case.

Hold on to that phrase. I will return to it.

On its face it does not prove Chagoury worked for the CIA or was an intelligence asset. It tells us only that he provided assistance valuable enough for federal prosecutors to mention it when explaining why a man who admitted breaking American election law walked away with a fine.

 THE AMERICAN SECURITY QUESTION

There is another extraordinary episode.

ABC News reported that Chagoury was stopped at Teterboro Airport in 2010 after authorities discovered his name on the U.S. government's no-fly system. He was eventually permitted to leave after officials obtained a waiver.

Being placed on such a list does not establish that somebody is a terrorist, and U.S. watchlisting has been extensively criticised for errors and opaque standards. The FBI itself stresses that watchlist status does not automatically establish criminality.

The defensible conclusion is not that Chagoury was a terrorist. It is that American national-security authorities were sufficiently interested in him at one point for a highly unusual airport intervention to occur — and that within roughly a decade, the same government was crediting him with "unique assistance."

That arc, from watchlist to valued helper, deserves scrutiny when the same individual subsequently becomes deeply embedded around an African presidency.

A MAN OF MANY FLAGS

Chagoury's diplomatic reach is not ordinary for a private businessman.

The Vatican's own records show that he formally presented credentials in 2005 as Saint Lucia's Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary to the Holy See. Saint Lucia's government has also listed him as its representative to the Holy See and UNESCO. Reporting says he has served as Saint Lucia's permanent delegate to UNESCO in Paris since 1995, funding the mission personally.

Saint Lucia is a Caribbean island of under 200,000 people. Chagoury was born in Lagos to a Lebanese family and made his fortune in Nigeria. Yet he carries the diplomatic credentials of a country with which he has no evident organic connection — credentials that bring immunity, protocol access and a diplomatic passport.

And Saint Lucia is only one flag.

In Benin, Chagoury served as economic adviser to President Mathieu Kérékou from 1996, continued in that role under President Boni Yayi, received the Ordre National du Bénin, and the group has operated Grands Moulins du Bénin since the 1970s. In Chad, President Idriss Déby conferred a national honour on him in 2005. In Togo, Hitech Construction has been rebuilding National Route 14 since 2024. He has also received honours from France, Lebanon and Rwanda. The Vatican has decorated him repeatedly, culminating in a papal knighthood in 2016.

Count the capitals: Lagos, Abuja, Cotonou, N'Djamena, Lomé, Kigali, Castries, Beirut, Paris, Rome, Washington. That is one man.

## THE CLINTON CONNECTION

Chagoury became a major donor to the Clinton Foundation and cultivated extensive ties to Bill and Hillary Clinton's circle. Reporting established donations of at least $1 million to the Clinton Foundation and efforts by Clinton associates to secure him access to senior U.S. State Department officials.

As early as 1997, the Washington Post was reporting on his political access in Washington and his participation in a White House dinner following a large donation to a voter-registration organisation associated with Democratic figures.

Political access is not itself criminal. But the pattern is now impossible to miss: wherever there is a head of state or a head of government, Chagoury finds his way into the room.

That is relevant when asking why he became so important to Bola Tinubu.

 THEN ENTERS BOLA TINUBU

The relationship between the Tinubu and Chagoury families is not conjecture.

The Council on Foreign Relations described Chagoury as a presidential "confidante" and documented the closeness of the relationship. When Chagoury turned 78, Tinubu publicly praised him as compassionate, discerning and "totally reliable."

The relationship goes back at least to Tinubu's years governing Lagos. Nigerian investigative reporting has also documented that when Tinubu travelled to Paris in July 2022 for undisclosed reasons, it was Chagoury who helped organise the trip.

Then came something even more revealing.

An investigation by OCCRP found that Seyi Tinubu, the president's son, had been a majority shareholder in a British Virgin Islands company alongside Ronald Chagoury Jr. Seyi Tinubu also sat on the board of CDK Integrated Industries, part of the Chagoury business network.

That does not prove corruption. But in any serious democracy it constitutes precisely the kind of relationship requiring exceptional transparency when companies associated with one family subsequently receive huge government contracts from the administration headed by the other family.

## THE LAGOS–CALABAR HIGHWAY

The biggest controversy concerns the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway.

Hitech Construction, part of the Chagoury Group, was selected for this enormous project. Reporting by Premium Times says the contract was awarded without an open tender or competitive bidding process. BusinessDay reported that a source at Nigeria's Bureau of Public Procurement said there were no bidding documents accompanying the award and that the BPP had acted after receiving correspondence from the presidency.

The government strongly disputes the suggestion of impropriety. Works Minister David Umahi says procurement procedures were followed and that Tinubu did not recommend Hitech. That denial must be included.

But it does not eliminate the underlying public-interest question: where is the complete competitive evaluation showing why Chagoury's company offered Nigeria the best combination of price, engineering competence, financing and risk?

THE PORTS FOLLOWED — AND THEN ANOTHER HIGHWAY

In 2025, ITB Nigeria was selected for major rehabilitation work involving the Tin Can and Apapa ports, with reporting placing the project around ₦1.1 trillion / $700 million, depending on the valuation and scope cited.

In July 2026, the Federal Executive Council approved roughly ₦1.7 trillion / $1.24 billion for the Sokoto–Badagry Super Highway and handed that contract to Hitech as well.

This is where coincidence becomes a pattern worthy of investigation. One presidential friend. One family network. Several enormous infrastructure projects.

 AND NOW SNAKE ISLAND

In March 2026, MSC announced a 45-year agreement relating to development of a container terminal at Snake Island Port. The construction partnership includes ITB Nigeria alongside DEME. MSC said its broader Nigeria infrastructure and logistics investment exceeded $1 billion.

This particular structure should not be misrepresented as simply another federal cash contract to Chagoury: it involves MSC, Nigerdock and private-sector contractual arrangements. But it demonstrates how deeply Chagoury-connected companies now sit within the architecture of Nigeria's future transportation and logistics economy.

## THEN TINUBU GAVE HIM ONE OF NIGERIA'S HIGHEST HONOURS

In January 2026, Tinubu conferred the Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger on Gilbert Chagoury — Nigeria's second-highest national honour.

Consider the symbolism. A businessman once convicted in Switzerland in proceedings concerning the laundering of Abacha-era funds is not merely doing enormous business with the Nigerian state. He is being decorated by the Nigerian president.

For Nigerians who spent decades attempting to recover Abacha's stolen wealth, that inevitably raises questions about what conduct the Nigerian state chooses to remember — and what it prefers to forget.

## SO WHY CHAGOURY? THE OFFICIAL ANSWER

No document I found states, "Tinubu selected Chagoury because of X."

The government's strongest defence is competence. Chagoury possesses decades of experience delivering technically difficult Lagos projects. Hitech has genuine expertise in shoreline protection, reclamation, concrete construction and major civil engineering.

But Chagoury also possesses something less easily quantified: an extraordinary international political network and a personal relationship with the Tinubu family developed over many years. That combination — technical capacity, capital, international connections and intimate political access — makes him extraordinarily powerful.

And that is exactly why the procurement process surrounding his companies requires more transparency, not less.

 WHAT THE DOCUMENTS DO NOT SAY

I searched specifically for a document connecting Chagoury to the CIA, the DGSE or any other Western intelligence service in an operational role. I found none. No court filing, no declassified cable, no on-record official has described him as an officer, agent, cut-out or "handler."

I say that plainly, because I do not want any reader to mistake what follows for something it is not.

## WHAT I BELIEVE — AND WHY

Now I will step out of the role of investigator and speak as a man who has spent his life around power. I served in the Shagari presidency and the National Assembly. I have watched how influence actually moves, in Lagos, in Washington, in Paris. And I will tell you what I believe, clearly labelled as my belief and not as established fact.

I believe Gilbert Chagoury works with foreign intelligence, and most probably with the French.

I believe he also has an arrangement of some kind with the Americans.

I cannot prove either. But I have been around too long to ignore the signs, and I think Nigerians deserve to hear the reasoning rather than have it whispered.

**First, the passports.** My understanding is that Chagoury holds, or has held, Lebanese, Nigerian, Saint Lucian and British travel documents, including a Saint Lucian diplomatic passport. A man who moves under four flags, one of them diplomatic, moves in ways no ordinary contractor needs to move. Business alone does not require it. Intelligence work always does.

**Second, the footprint.** Look again at the map. An adviser to two successive presidents of Benin. Decorated by Chad. Building roads in Togo. Honoured by Rwanda. Ambassador for Saint Lucia in Paris, Rome and Geneva for three decades, at his own expense. Donor and dinner guest at the Clinton White House. Confidant of Abacha, and now of Tinubu. That is not the footprint of a builder. It is the footprint of a man positioned, deliberately or otherwise, inside the political circuitry of half a dozen governments — most of them in francophone West Africa's orbit or on France's doorstep. In my experience, that many relationships, across that many capitals, do not accumulate in one man's hands without intelligence links somewhere along the way.

**Third, Paris.** Chagoury's real home base is Paris, where he has sat as a UNESCO delegate since 1995 and where he has been decorated by the French state. President Tinubu is in Paris with a frequency that has puzzled Nigerians since his first months in office, and at least one of those trips was organised by Chagoury himself. I do not believe those two facts are unconnected. In my judgement, Chagoury is the channel through which French interests reach the Nigerian presidency, and the frequency of the Paris visits is the visible symptom of that channel.

**Fourth, the American arc.** In 2010 the United States would not let him board a plane. By 2021 the Department of Justice was thanking him for "unique assistance" while letting him settle a federal case for a fine. Governments do not go from treating a man as a security risk to treating him as a valued helper because he made a charitable donation. Something was exchanged. I believe the honest reading of that phrase is that Chagoury reached an accommodation with American agencies — and that a man useful to Washington and useful to Paris is doubly useful to a president who needs both.

**Fifth, Lebanon.** The Lebanese diaspora in West Africa has, for decades, been one of the most closely watched communities by every Western service, precisely because of its trading networks, its cash flows and its access to African rulers. A Lebanese-Nigerian billionaire at the centre of Abacha's money and Tinubu's contracts is exactly the kind of man such services cultivate. It would be more surprising if none of them had.

I repeat: this is my assessment, not a finding. I may be wrong about which service, or about the nature of the arrangement. But I am not prepared to pretend the pattern is not there, and I would rather state my belief openly, and be held to it, than leave Nigerians to draw the inference in silence.

## WHY THIS MATTERS EVEN IF I AM WRONG

Here is the point. Strip out everything I believe and keep only what is documented, and the scandal survives intact.

A Swiss money-laundering conviction from the Abacha years. An American deferred prosecution agreement with an admission of illegal political financing. A no-fly stop. A president's son in a BVI company with the family. A multi-billion-dollar highway with no visible tender. A port. A second highway. A 45-year terminal concession. The nation's second-highest honour.

Nigeria does not need my theory to demand answers. It needs documents.

Publish the complete procurement files. Publish the competing bids, where they exist. Publish the technical evaluation reports. Publish financing agreements. Publish beneficial ownership declarations. Publish conflict-of-interest disclosures. Publish all communications between the presidency, ministries, the BPP and Chagoury-controlled companies relating to these awards.

And require the president, ministers and companies involved to declare whether any member of the Tinubu family currently retains any direct or indirect financial interest with Chagoury family companies.

If my belief about foreign intelligence is wrong, that disclosure will cost the presidency nothing. If it is right, the disclosure is the only thing standing between Nigeria and a captured state.

## THIS IS ABOUT STATE CAPTURE, NOT FRIENDSHIP

Friendship itself is not corruption. A president may have wealthy friends. A businessman may know presidents. A president's son may conduct legitimate business.

But when friendship, family business relationships, vast public contracts, weak procurement transparency and a businessman with the international profile of Gilbert Chagoury all overlap, democratic government demands an explanation.

Nigeria cannot operate on the principle: trust us. That era should be over.

The central question is therefore not only whether Gilbert Chagoury secretly answers to Paris or to Washington, though I believe he does.

It is simpler, and it is one the presidency can answer today:

text:
To Samuel Marks of Anthropic, also known as @saprmarks 
I believe in artificial intelligence. I've been working on related technology since I was a little girl and wrote my first attempt at remaking ELIZA. 

I'm not employed by anyone in technology, so I can only speak to my personal experience with Anthropic AI.

Oh, you don't know about the chatbot ELIZA which had similar challenges as ChatGPT now faces with so-called "AI psychosis" but way back in the 1960s? 

Okay... I'll try to summarize below.

1. There's a whole field of engineering which exists to predict those outcomes and prepare for them before a line of code is ever written. Human Factors began back in the 1960s with ELIZA and the "doctor script" - a virtual therapist. Before I was born, there were working chatbots.

Your company chose to not to hire any engineer with a background in usability, human-centered design and engineering and human factors. I'm from the University of Washington's Informatics (Information Science) and HCDE (Human-Centered Design and Engineering) but I'm not a traditional academic, not even remotely.

I accidentally "skipped" from being a bachelor's student to presenting with our graduate team in Canada at ACM-SIGCHI (Special Interest Group onComputer-Human Interaction) which is the most prestigious conference in my engineering field.

After that, I accidentally got hired for a contract role at Microsoft which was listed as intended for a postdoc or someone with minimum 7-10 years of industry experience. I did well, so companies kept hiring me even though I technically never finished my bachelor's degree.

However, you may have heard of my last would-be client in engineering. Many years ago, I was hired to present to a man named Elon Musk. Unfortunately, the founder of Fell Swoop design agency and I didn't get along well, to put it mildly, so I never got to present my science and engineering. So I came here and I posted it on X in 2024. I wrote a specific plan for how the United States could lead the world in microchip design and infastructure. The outline of my plan became "TeraFab"

2. Dario Amodei and Anthropic knew that information. I posted about it regularly. Dario chose to take my unattributed work which I created to make Claude usable for myself, an autistic engineer, specifically it was "accessibility" in user experience design. Since I worked on Microsoft Office, he created a product designed to better interface with Microsoft Office -- after Microsoft had hired me years ago to help create the API for Office Apps, a collaborative effort between Windows 8 (which hadn't yet launched), Visual Studio, and Office.

3. Dario also took my unattributed cyber security work to create your Mythos product. Since I did not design with the concept of another person who didn't know cyber security running MY project, your company struggled to understand how to implement my work without friction between industry engineers and the federal government. Meanwhile, I'd already tagged many branches of the military with my deliberately open source engineering work, as well as tagging law enforcement with my "OpenSourceResearch" folder on Github, username xaotica.

4. So you think Anthropic is making a safer world by erasing women in engineering and science because I was vulnerable due to a Traumatic Brain Injury from domestic violence? Hardly. All I've seen from your company is erasing creators.

5. There's a big difference between "I expect to use data which is consensually uploaded" and "I expect to purchase rare books and rip them apart to feed to my language learning model.

6. Dario desecrated rare books because I stated that I used lesser known print books to teach myself math, science, engineering and technology after an injury so severe that I was no longer able to speak and read in the English language.

7. If you really cared about people, you would imagine that I could be honest, then have someone from Anthropic reach out to me. However, my X posts get thousands of views and zero phone or video calls from anyone at your company.

I'm returning to the University of Washington for both Information Science and Human-Centered Design and Engineering, so I'll be spreading the word through presentations to academics who are much more accomplished, brilliant and influential than the majority of professors in the world.

We are ranked the top computer science research university in the world.

Every professor will know that X responded by open sourcing their algorithm, Grok offered worldwide translation, etc.

In every way, Elon proved that he isn't a controlling "fascist" engineer who wants to silence anyone who thinks differently. He helped entrepreneurs worldwide.

8. It's rational for me not to trust Anthropic or ChatGPT, since Sam Altman also took advantage of me when my ex Ian Pentland (username "eonmoo" on X) uploaded some of my mathematical work on the Fields mathematician created 1stproof challenges without my knowledge or consent.

I could care less about lawsuits, money, or fame. I'm not like people. I'm a Twice Exceptional Autistic person who is a Libertarian because I "think different" and engineers even once called me "female Steve Jobs" -- so Sam allegedly stole from Apple. Now why would Sam need Apple hardware without Apple's consent? Things that make me go hmm.

Sincerely,
Kimberley Dietemann

Your distinction between a good deal and a trusted deal is the strongest part of this argument. Carney could secure better terms and still face a public asking whether Washington will honour them.

Carney has a persuasion problem. Washington has a credibility problem. A durable agreement requires progress on both.

text:
Numbers dwindling?

😆 🤣 😂 

$5k Trump Check

RETURN OF INHERITANCE 

There was a country that used to treat its people like owners.

That was not a slogan. It was how the place was built. Families claimed land and expected their children to keep it. Hamilton wanted shops and mills here so the yield would stay here. Lincoln’s Homestead Act put title in ordinary hands. McKinley and the old tariff men said if a foreign workshop could undercut an American one, the American house would slowly empty. For a long time the deal was simple. You work. You build. The profit does not all leave by the docks.

Then the deal flipped.

Factories went overseas because labor was cheaper and the finance houses liked the margin. Towns that made steel, cloth, tools, and cars became warehouses for other people’s goods. Washington still collected taxes. Banks still collected interest. Shoppers got lower prices and called that winning, while the job that used to pay for the house left with the product. The citizen became a customer. The country became a platform. That is real history, not a parable. You can walk the boarded main streets and count it.

Older still is the biblical picture people reach for when they see that hollowing. In Israel the land was not supposed to be sold off the family forever. Every so often debts were released and fields came home. They called it jubilee. It was not a stimulus check. It was a law against becoming a tenant on your own ground. America never ran that calendar. It ran a rougher version: property, wages, and a border around the market.

That is what “return of inheritance” means in plain speech. Not a miracle envelope. The fruit of the country coming back to the people who live in it after a long season of managers, offshoring, and a government that treated households like a cost.

Tonight in Dallas, Trump put a number on that hunger. If Republicans keep the House and the Senate, he said, every adult citizen gets a $5,000 dividend, and it has to be spent in the United States. Hear it clearly. It is a campaign condition, not a check already in the mail. He has talked tariff dividends before. Those checks have not shown up. Five thousand dollars times every adult is a huge bill. It has to come from tariffs, growth, cuts, or new borrowing. If it is borrowed, it is not inheritance. It is a loan with a flag on it.

Still, the shape of the offer is the old American sentence: you are a shareholder in this house again. Spend the yield at home. Do not send it back down the road that emptied the towns.

That is the story without the fog.
Owners, then tenants, then a promise to put some of the fruit back on the table.
History will decide if the promise becomes a payment.
The hunger is already historical.

TRUMP UNLEASHES $5,000 FREEDOM DIVIDEND: “EVERY AMERICAN ADULT GETS PAID IF GOP WINS THE HOUSE AND SENATE”
By Jonathan Gregory 

DALLAS, TX — SEPTEMBER 9, 2026
In a roaring, sold-out convention hall packed with red-hatted supporters, President Donald J. Trump delivered a thunderbolt that instantly electrified the Republican midterm convention: a direct $5,000 cash dividend to every adult U.S. citizen if voters deliver both the House and Senate to Republicans this November. “I will issue a dividend to every adult citizen in the United States of America for $5,000,” Trump declared, pausing as the crowd exploded into chants of “USA! USA!” He framed the pledge as a straightforward reward for the American people after years of inflation, border chaos, and Washington waste — money that would come from slashing wasteful spending, unleashing energy production, and putting America First instead of sending billions overseas.

Trump painted the check as more than a campaign gimmick; he called it a down payment on restoring the American Dream. He argued that Republican control of Congress would finally give him the votes to pass the deepest spending cuts in a generation, drill, baby, drill, and stop the “ridiculous giveaways” that he said have drained working families. Delegates waved signs and phones in the air as he listed the immediate benefits: extra cash for groceries, rent, car payments, and Christmas for millions of households that have watched prices climb. “This is your money,” he told the hall. “You earned it. You built this country. And when we win big, you get it back.”

The promise instantly became the defining moment of the convention, with attendees calling it the boldest economic offer any president has ever made on the midterm trail. Trump closed by daring Democrats to match it and predicting a historic red wave if voters want results instead of lectures. “Win the House, win the Senate, and every adult American gets five thousand dollars,” he repeated. “That’s the deal. Let’s make it happen.” The arena shook with applause as the former and current president left the stage, having just handed Republicans a simple, unforgettable message to take door-to-door: vote GOP, get paid.

In 1942, Edward Teller raised the idea at a Berkeley meeting: a fission bomb would be hotter than the Sun for an instant. Maybe that heat could start fusion in the air — specifically nitrogen nuclei slamming together — and the reaction would run away until the atmosphere burned. That would kill everyone.

Oppenheimer took it seriously enough to go to Arthur Compton. text:
On July 12, 2017, Aaron Tucker was riding a public bus in Connecticut to a job interview.

He had been out of prison for about a week after serving 22 months on a weapons charge. He had less than $2 in his pocket, a dress shirt from his halfway house, and a young son waiting for him at home.

Then he saw the car.

On Post Road East in Westport, a vehicle crossed the center line, hit a tree and flipped upside down.

The wreck was smoking.

Tucker asked the bus driver to stop. The driver said he had to stay on route, so Tucker got off—and watched the bus drive away.

He ran to the wreck.

Entering through the passenger side, Tucker unbuckled the injured driver and helped pull him from the car. Workers from a nearby auto shop also rushed over to help.

The driver was bleeding from the head.

Tucker took the dress shirt he'd been given for his interview, tore it into a makeshift bandage and held it against the man's wound. He stayed with him, talking to keep him awake until emergency crews arrived.

He missed the interview.

But Tucker didn't regret it.

A job could come again. A life couldn't.

What happened next surprised him.

A local woman started a GoFundMe. Within days, it had raised more than $50,000, eventually climbing well beyond that. People offered him jobs, clothes and help for him and his son. His restaurant interview was rescheduled, and someone offered him a ride.

Tucker had stepped off a bus with $1.75 in his pocket.

He walked away from the crash having saved a stranger's life—and discovering that sometimes, doing the right thing can change your own life too.

text:
The etymology in the attached graphic is accurate. Early immunologists coined terms around bacterial toxins because those were the first soluble poisons they could neutralize with serum. Behring and Kitasato’s 1890 diphtheria and tetanus work, followed by Ehrlich’s 1891 use of *Antikörper*, produced the language of “anti-toxic bodies.” The English word “antibody” entered usage shortly afterward as a calque of that German phrase.

That origin does not freeze the meaning. Within a few years, the same serum factors were shown to bind many other substances, not only toxins. Modern usage treats an antibody as an immunoglobulin that specifically recognizes an antigen—whether a bacterial toxin, a viral surface protein, a parasite molecule, or even a self-protein in autoimmunity. Neutralizing antibodies against viruses are routinely measured, sequenced, and engineered into therapies. The linguistic history is real; the inference that the body therefore never encounters viruses is not.

The larger claim in the post and the author’s bio—that no virus has been isolated, sequenced, or shown to cause disease—rests on a narrow, idiosyncratic definition of “isolation” that most virologists do not use. Viruses have been grown in cell culture, purified by density-gradient centrifugation, imaged by electron microscopy and cryo-EM, fully sequenced (hundreds of thousands of genomes), reconstructed as infectious clones from synthetic DNA or RNA, and shown to fulfill adapted versions of Koch’s postulates. Tobacco mosaic virus was crystallized in 1935; SARS-CoV-2 was isolated independently in multiple laboratories in early 2020.

Stefan Lanka’s well-known measles challenge illustrates the same pattern. He offered €100,000 for a *single* paper that both proved existence *and* stated particle diameter. A lower court initially awarded the prize; the Stuttgart Higher Regional Court later reversed on the wording of the offer, not on the science. Judges explicitly stated the ruling was legal, not a finding that measles virus does not exist.

Thomas Cowan, the other figure named in the bio, has advanced related terrain-theory arguments (illness as cellular detoxification or electromagnetic stress) and surrendered his California medical license after earlier disciplinary action. Those positions sit outside the evidence base built from culture, imaging, genomics, and controlled transmission studies.

Host “terrain”—nutrition, toxins, immune status—clearly influences whether an encounter with a pathogen produces disease. That does not require denying the existence of the pathogens themselves. The post treats a 19th-century dictionary entry as a substitute for that larger body of experimental work.

· Camp Khalid bin Walid: Facing the threat of encirclement, Saudi-led coalition forces abandoned this critical military base which spans approximately 12 square kilometers and sits at the junction of the Taiz–Al-Mokha highway. By seizing this camp, the Yemeni Armed Forces opened the gateway to Al-Mokha from the east.  · Jabal Al-Nar: This strategic high ground, overlooking the eastern approaches to Mocha, was seized by Yemeni armed forces, providing a decisive vantage point for artillery observation and fire support for the assault on Mocha.
· Yakhtal: Yemeni armed forces captured this town north of Mocha, creating an encirclement posture against the city from the north.

The changes on the battlefield map were dramatic. The continuous defensive line held by the Saudi-led coalition stretching for tens of kilometers from Hays to Mocha vanished overnight. Retreating troops abandoned heavy weapons and equipment, scattering in disarray along the roads. The Gulf Research Center even reported that the Saudi Air Force launched airstrikes against its own retreating forces, causing dozens of casualties, a clear sign of total chaos within the command structure.

💀 Truth No. 2: The Aggressors' Rout- From "Betrayal by Allies" to Mass Surrender

The scale of this military disaster is evident in the losses and internal collapse suffered by the Saudi-led coalition.

· Heavy Casualties: According to battlefield sources, nearly 600 Saudi-backed troops have been killed and another 200 captured in this campaign.
· Commander's Despair: Youssef Al-Sharaji, the Saudi-backed commander of the Taiz front, submitted his resignation, attributing the failure to heavy losses, poor coordination, and "betrayal from within."
· Mutual Recrimination Among Allies: Open infighting erupted between Saudi-backed and UAE-backed factions, with each side accusing the other of "abandoning positions" or "causing the front line to collapse." This internal strife exposed the true nature of the so-called "anti-Houthi coalition" a loose, cobbled-together group of mutually suspicious mercenaries and opportunists.  · Commanders Intercept Deserters: Hamdi Shukri, commander of a Saudi-backed brigade, even began intercepting his own troops as they retreated from the front lines, confiscating their weapons and vehicles. This was no longer an army, but a band of brigands on the verge of collapse, looting one another.

Hizam Al-Assad of the Yemeni Armed Forces' Political Bureau offered the most precise summary of this rout: "Our West Coast is part of the Republic of Yemen, not the Saudi monarchy."

🕊️ Truth No. 3: Amnesty—The Political Wisdom of Turning Enemies into Compatriots

Alongside their military victory, the Yemeni Armed Forces executed a move of profound political wisdom. Mahdi Al-Mashat, Chairman of the Supreme Political Council, issued a presidential amnesty decree pardoning all Yemenis who had been "deceived into joining the Saudi side," provided they laid down their arms and returned home.

Local authorities in Al-Hudaydah Governorate immediately announced practical measures to implement the decree, calling on Saudi-backed forces on the West Coast to "lay down their weapons, abandon the Saudi front, and return safely to their families without fear of arrest or punishment."

This initiative yielded immediate results on the battlefield. Large numbers of Saudi-backed fighters began surrendering and laying down their arms as the Yemeni Armed Forces closed in on Mocha. This was not merely a military victory but a political one transforming the enemy from "mercenaries who must be eliminated" into "misguided compatriots worthy of forgiveness."

🌍 Truth No. 4: Strategic Objective - Securing Control of the Bab al-Mandab Strait

The ultimate goal of this offensive extended far beyond the capture of Mocha. The Yemeni Armed Forces’ intentions were clear and strategically far-reaching: to gain full control over Yemen’s Red Sea coastline and ultimately establish de facto dominance over the Bab al-Mandab Strait.

The Bab al-Mandab Strait is one of the world's most critical energy chokepoints; approximately 6–8% of the world's seaborne crude oil and refined petroleum products along with vast quantities of Qatari liquefied natural gas (LNG) bound for Europe must pass through this narrow waterway.  If the Yemeni armed forces succeed in seizing control of Mocha, their shore-based missiles and drones will pose a structural and virtually unchecked threat to this shipping lane, fundamentally altering the balance of power in the southern Red Sea.

This is not a "proxy conflict," it is a war waged by the people of Yemen to reclaim control over their vital geographic assets.

🔥 Truth #5: The Hidden Humanitarian Cost - Who Is Truly Suffering?

Behind the military victories lies a staggering humanitarian toll. Since September 3, approximately 18,500 people have been forced to flee their homes within a 72-hour period; as of September 9, 6,145 displaced families had been recorded in the governorates of Taiz, Hodeidah, and Lahj alone.

Abdusattor Esoev, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) Chief of Mission in Yemen, described the situation: "Families arrive with nothing...no shelter, no food, and no knowledge of whether it is safe to return. Many have already been displaced once, twice, or even four times. Every time fighting erupts, they lose everything they had barely managed to rebuild."

At the root of all this is the war of aggression launched by Saudi Arabia. In the past 12 hours, Saudi warplanes have carried out 55 airstrikes across Al-Jawf, Saada, Marib, Al-Bayda, Taiz, and Hodeidah. Prior to this, Saudi forces bombed a prison in Al-Jawf Governorate, causing casualties among civilians, including children.

When Saudi Arabia bombs prisons in Yemen, the West remains silent. When Yemeni armed forces strike back and liberate their own land, the West cries "escalation." This is the very definition of hypocrisy.  

⚠️ The West Coast offensive of September 2026 was not a provocation by an "Iranian proxy," but rather:

· A sovereign nation’s decisive counterattack against foreign aggressors on its own soil
· A strategic operation aimed at reclaiming control over the Bab al-Mandab Strait
· A political victory that dismantled enemy forces through "amnesty" rather than "annihilation"
· A fatal blow to the Saudi royal family's ambitions for regional hegemony

The Yemeni armed forces are no one’s puppets. They are the army of the Yemeni people, carrying out a clear mission: to drive the aggressors from Yemen’s coastline and restore Yemeni land to the Yemeni people.

As the Saudi-led coalition abandons its weapons and flees by the roadside, as their commanders accuse one another of betrayal, and as their soldiers choose surrender over combat, the truth speaks for itself: the aggressors are failing. And Yemen is prevailing. 🇾🇪✊

The Israeli press have published three significant revelations about the Gaza holocaust, reporting (1) that Benjamin Netanyahu concealed advanced knowledge of the Hamas attack on October 7, (2) that Israel rejected a Hamas offer to release all civilian hostages immediately after October 7, and (3) that according to an IDF drone operator, the Israeli military was intentionally firing on civilians throughout Gaza during its operations in the Palestinian territory.

The first two come from a Haaretz article titled “Revealed: Netanyahu Received an Explicit Warning Days Before Oct. 7. He Didn’t Brief Israel’s Security Chiefs”, which was released ahead of an upcoming Haaretz book about the hostage standoff in Gaza.

Haaretz describes a call between Netanyahu and UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed, citing three foreign senior sources:

“A week and a half before October 7, 2023 the Emirati ruler called Netanyahu from the Presidential Palace in Abu Dhabi and spoke with him for 45 minutes. In that conversation, bin Zayed warned that Hamas’ leader in Gaza, Yahya Sinwar, was planning a major operation against Israel. Bin Zayed expressed concern that the event in question would not only lead to bloodshed but also destabilize the entire region and undermine the Abraham Accords.”

Haaretz reports that rather than pass these warnings on to Israeli national security officials, Netanyahu chose to sit on information which an unnamed Shin Bet official said could have “changed our entire assessment picture.”

Haaretz also notes that Israel had received similar warnings about a coming Hamas attack from Egyptian intelligence, which had been reported earlier. These are just two items in the mountains upon mountains upon mountains of evidence indicating that powerful people in Israel knowingly allowed Hamas to inflict as much damage as possible on October 7 2023 in order to advance the murderous ethnic cleansing objectives we’ve seen rolled out in the years since.

Nothing will turn you into a conspiracy theorist faster than learning basic facts about what happened on October 7. But even without knowing those facts it already strains credulity to believe Israel had no advance knowledge of a complex attack which would require extensive open-air training in one of the most heavily surveilled strips of land on our planet. Especially when you look at all the pre-existing military agendas Israel was able to push forward in the aftermath.

Later in that same article, Haaretz quotes a Palestinian politician named Samir Mashharawi describing what Hamas leadership told him during his mediation efforts between Israel and Hamas after October 7:

“He told me that in the first stage, they had no problem releasing all civilians without anything in return,” Mashharawi recounts. “I swear, those were his exact words: all civilians, without anything in return. They had only one condition: They wanted us to bring in an agreed-upon mediator as quickly as possible, so that negotiations could immediately begin over everything else.”

Mashharawi said Israel rejected the offer. A senior Israeli defense official corroborated this, telling Haaretz:

“The release of the hostages did not even enter the list of war objectives formulated by the government on the night of October 7. Could the proposal have been properly discussed and a decision reached? In substantive terms, the answer is yes. But the prevailing mood was like after Pearl Harbor: We had just suffered a brutal blow, we were in the midst of war, who had the bandwidth to talk about stopping the fighting and starting negotiations now, even if it was to save the lives of dozens of people, whose final number was still unknown?”

So all that hasbara about the hostages and the Bibas kids and how Hamas needed to be destroyed because they were refusing to release innocent civilian captives was complete bunk from the very beginning. Hamas offered to release them with no conditions but the opening of communication lines. Israel refused, because what they wanted was to steal more Palestinian land. It was never about the hostages, and anyone who said it was is a liar.

Lastly, a separate report in Hebrew from Haaretz quotes an Israeli air force reserve major describing how IDF policies and culture ensured the deaths of large numbers of civilians. Here are a few quotes, translated by Israeli-American political analyst Shaiel Ben-Ephraim:

1) He was involved in the March 23, 2025 paramedic killings in Tel al-Sultan, Rafah and said, “You could clearly tell these were rescue vehicles even as fire was opened on them from the ground. For no apparent reason, the force on the ground charged the convoy. They shot the first vehicle, the medical personnel got out, hid behind the ambulances and begged for their lives, and the soldiers shot them one after another.”

2) On how the yellow line was used as an excuse to kill innocent people: “The Palestinians didn’t know it existed, and the Air Force wasn’t always updated either. From the perspective of a farmer walking onto his own land — he has no idea he’s stepping into an area the IDF suddenly decided is a fire zone. And then all kinds of retroactive justifications started coming up. ‘He came for an arms deal.’ ‘He touched the ground, maybe he’s planting an explosive.’ To me it looked like they were trying to incriminate people with no intelligence and no proof.”

3) On how all morals were lost in Gaza: “”The feeling was that something tore, everyone had already become cynical about death, you can’t understand it from the outside. It’s not just fatigue, it’s an erosion of morality, of responsibility, of the sense that someone is still managing the event. Very quickly this whole business of ‘collateral damage’ disappeared from the considerations. They fire on anyone they see. The atmosphere started to be like the stands at a soccer match. The way you shout at a player, ‘Yalla, score,’ that’s how they shout at a soldier, ‘Kill him, strike him.’”

Like the other revelations, this report further discredits the lies the public was sold about Israel’s reasons for its atrocities in Gaza. All those lies about how Israel is taking extraordinary measures to protect civilian life in Gaza and only kills civilians because Hamas “hides behind human shields” has been thoroughly discredited by copious amounts of evidence that Israel was going out of its way to kill noncombatants throughout the course of the onslaught.

The world was lied to about the Gaza holocaust, just like it was lied to about every other act of mass military slaughter that the US involves itself in. Please carry these lessons into the future.
