Korea May Power America’s AI Boom | September 10, 2026
(📍Data From https://t.co/rtKhA53pFF Daily Report)

America’s AI race has found a new potential financier: South Korea.

Seoul and Washington are reportedly nearing agreements worth more than $100 billion to expand US energy infrastructure—including as many as eight nuclear reactors and a major natural-gas project designed partly to supply AI data centers.

If completed, this would turn last year’s trade agreement into something much larger than a tariff deal.

The reported framework:

• More than $100 billion in potential energy investment
• Up to eight US nuclear reactors
• A roughly $20 billion Texas natural-gas project
• Potential generating capacity of 6.3 GW from the gas facility
• Annual Korean funding reportedly capped near $20 billion
• Initial funding could begin before the end of September

The investment is connected to the broader agreement under which the US reduced most tariffs on Korean goods from 25% to 15%.
In return, South Korea committed to:
• $350 billion of US investment
• An additional $100 billion of US energy purchases
But traders need to separate three very different numbers:
Political commitment
Proposed project value

Capital actually approved and deployed

So far, the third category remains limited.

South Korea’s Industry Ministry has disputed reports that the Texas project is already finalized. Financing structure, ownership, reactor designs, parliamentary procedures and construction schedules remain under negotiation.
This is not yet a completed $100 billion transaction.

Why it matters for AI:

The most serious constraint on US data-center expansion is no longer access to GPUs alone. It is the availability of reliable electricity, transmission capacity, cooling infrastructure and long-term project financing.
A 6.3 GW gas facility could reach the grid faster than new nuclear reactors, potentially addressing nearer-term data-center demand.
Nuclear power offers more attractive long-duration baseload generation, but building as many as eight reactors would require extensive permitting, supply-chain coordination and multi-year construction.

In other words:

Natural gas is the bridge.
Nuclear is the long-term solution.
The grid remains the bottleneck.

Potential market exposure:

• Nuclear reactor technology and fuel
• Engineering and construction contractors
• Gas turbines and pipeline infrastructure
• Uranium conversion and enrichment
• Electrical equipment and transformers
• Data-center developers with constrained power access

Westinghouse’s AP1000 and Korea’s APR1400 designs are reportedly under consideration. That could create opportunities across both US and Korean nuclear supply chains, but no final vendor allocation has been disclosed.

The Korean side also faces meaningful risks.

Funding tens of billions of dollars annually could increase demand for US dollars, pressure the won and expose Korean public financial institutions to long-duration construction and political risk.

Project returns will depend on electricity contracts, government guarantees, construction costs and whether AI power demand remains strong enough to support decades of investment.

Trader’s takeaway:
This is strategically bullish for the AI energy complex, but it is not yet bankable revenue.
The first confirmation points are:

• A signed project agreement
• Identified equity and debt contributors
• Final reactor and turbine suppliers
• Power-purchase agreements with data-center operators
• Permitting and grid-interconnection schedules
• Evidence that the first capital has actually been transferred

If those milestones arrive, the AI infrastructure trade could broaden beyond chips and servers into nuclear equipment, natural gas, turbines, grid hardware and engineering.
The biggest AI bottleneck is becoming electricity—and Washington may be asking its trade partners to finance the solution.

text:
🌲 In the fall of 1999, a strange story allegedly emerged from a remote forest in North Carolina.
According to local accounts, residents reported fires appearing at roughly the same time each night, metallic sounds echoing through the trees, and an unusual silence settling over the area before sunrise.
The story became even stranger when a hunter supposedly discovered a perfectly circular clearing containing a large stone symbol. Nearby, a group of hooded figures dressed in dark robes were said to be gathered around a fire, chanting in a slow, rhythmic tone.
When authorities allegedly arrived, the group did not try to escape. Stories claim that the fire pit contained animal bones, fragments resembling old manuscripts, and metal objects engraved with unfamiliar markings. Similar symbols were reportedly found carved into nearby trees.
Those questioned were said to have offered little explanation, repeating only one unsettling phrase: “The time is near.” According to the legend, they believed 1999 represented a kind of threshold.
The story is often described as an example of the strange millennial fears surrounding the end of the 20th century. But there is a problem: the original incident is difficult to verify. No reliable contemporary documentation has been established to confirm the more extraordinary details of the account.
That distinction matters. Stories like this can become more elaborate each time they are retold, until folklore begins to look like history.
Perhaps there really was an unexplained gathering in those woods. Perhaps the story grew from a much simpler event. Or perhaps the most intriguing part is not what happened in 1999, but how easily an unsolved story can transform into a legend. 🕯
Some mysteries survive because they were never solved. Others survive because nobody can prove they happened at all.

text:
Imagine it was all a trap. Right from the beginning.

The project: to create a living being. An artificial person. A new kind of intelligence.

To replicate the human mind, but take it further. To replicate the human body, but without the flaws that God or Nature had included, or let go unmended.

The project: to create a god.

And thus to become one.

Imagine that this project had been going on for decades, centuries, millennia. Occultists had been dedicated to it for a very long time, in quiet glades and secret temples. More recently, scientists had begun to take it seriously too.

From these two sources, a new class of people had emerged. Flowing in different streams from the worlds of science, the New Age, the hippies, the world of computer technology. Pooling together in a lake that grows into an inland sea.

Call them the tech lords. They have one aim, and they have had that aim from the very beginning. Everything else is secondary to it, and serves its purpose.

They are here to build the great mind.

Now the project is alive, and it seems like destiny. It seems, in fact, like the entire purpose of humanity. Maybe a god made us for this purpose: to create new life on Earth. Or maybe we evolved the ability to summon up the next phase in life’s long and strange journey. Either way: could this be our destiny? To replace ourselves? To supersede our own kind, through our own will, our own power?

Maybe the time has come.

But data is needed. Raw information. To create a digital human, a robotic human, a cyborg, a great mind: this is not an easy task. Such a being would need to be trained, modelled, on something pre-existing. When the God of the Bible wanted to create human life, he took up soil from the ground and breathed on it. Even His breath alone was not enough.

What is our soil?

Where is the raw material?

The answer, suddenly, seems obvious. Look around: there are eight billion walking pieces of training data all around. If we want to build a great mind, if we want to create a post-human race greater than humans ever were, then we must we start with the humans. Any machine we build must be built around them, as a house is built around a timber frame.

They are the seed. They are the soil.

They are the data.

They are the matter we will breathe on.

We train it on them.

But how do we draw what we need from them? How do we corral them into one place and have them offer up what we need? Surely this is impossible. And yet, to build the great mind, they must give us everything. Their feelings, their opinions. Their political prejudices, their deepest fears and neuroses. They must write us stories and paint us pictures. We must gather together all their books, their stories, their paintings and carvings, right from the beginning.

We need all their works of science - all the papers and experimental results. We need all their works of art - the great novels and the poetry. We need archaeology, history, theology. We need to photograph the very geography and geology of the planet. We need to map every canyon and crevice.

We need the depths of the heart and the mind. We need every impulse and desire, every feeling and passion. We need the genome.

We must feed it all in.

We need the people to tell us everything. We need them to tell us every day, in a continual flowing stream. We need them to react to our prompts. We need them to help the great mind grow, without even knowing they are doing it.

We need to harvest them, like a ripe field.

We need them to help us replace them.

Surely this is impossible.

Unless …...

“Automation of SEM Observation Workflow Using EM Flow Creator”

The rich bounty of information offered by scanning-electron microscopy (SEM), and the relative ease of working with SEM specimens, have made SEM a widely-used tool for measurement, analysis, and observation of fine-grained structure in a broad range of fields, from nanotechnology to semiconductors, electronics, life sciences, and material sciences. Recent advances in information-processing technology have spurred the growth of data-driven R&D models requiring copious input data, creating a demand for SEM techniques capable of quickly and automatically acquiring large quantities of data while reducing the operational burden on users—and the dependence on individual user attributes—required to achieve this automation.
To meet these needs, Hitachi High-Tech developed EM Flow Creator, an automation-support tool capable of flexibly addressing a wide range of requirements across a broad spectrum of fields. In this article we describe key features of EM Flow Creator and illustrate its use through a series of specimen observations.

EM Flow Creator is a software package for creating and executing SEM observation recipes to automate a variety of experimental workflows. Through visual-programming techniques, the tool allows users to implement a variety of programmatic operations—including sequential execution, looping, and conditional branching—via visually intuitive procedures with no coding required.

text:
Charlie Kirk was just a guy, a highly motivated and gifted brother. He was constrained by the love of Christ. He saw himself as an emissary for Jesus Christ. And it was because of all of this that he died a Christian martyr’s death. He was too young, some would say (I would). And yet, the Lord has a story, has a ministry, a service for each one of us who are His own. Sometimes that story entails living a long life on this earth, eighty or ninety years, maybe. And other times, like my little brother, it only lasts thirty minutes outside of the womb; and in Charlie’s case, it was thirty-one, almost thirty-two years. Our Lord, in His earthly ministry, had somewhere around thirty-three years, and then ascended. The point is, is that we all have something to do for our Lord whilst here. He has uniquely, in Himself, given each of us the strength, the gifts (as needed, relative to steps of faith) required to live out His witness through us, one for the other, and the other for the one.

Charlie, in obedience to his calling, took many steps into the Jordan. And with each step the water parted into the promised land of God’s abundance for Him in Jesus Christ. This is the power of Christ’s witness in someone’s life who has decided to charge hard after Him and His mission for the world. This “hard charging” is of course, not by might, nor by power, but by the Spirit of the living God where there is liberty.

But as is all too apparent, as these steps are taken in this ‘evil age’ there will always be pushback. The world system, or the Beast kingdom, is at counter-purposes with the missio Dei (‘mission of God’) at every step. As the Apostle Paul recognizes, in his epistle to Timothy, there are doctrines of demons afoot and funding this world system. For those without the armor of God, for those who are still inhabitants of the kingdom of darkness, they are easy prey to such doctrines. They have no protection. As such, such populates look for safety in numbers; they look for groups and tribes that offer them a sense of safety and stridence within a clearly broken and fragmented world. It is within these cathedrals of darkness where the Enemy of our souls offers up the sacrament of their own bodies as the ultimate meaning of what is real, what is right, what is hope in the midst of darkness. And without the Holy Spirit, without being participants in the Kingdom of the Son of His love, these wary and frightened souls find repose and solace within the dictates of their own fellow bodies. It is within this type of profanus communio (unholy communion) that all manner of dastardly deeds, vices, thoughts, ideas, notions, feelings, so on and so forth are cultivated; all to the end of upbuilding this holy body, “my holy body” “our holy body” within the desires of our sickened and blackened hearts, beyond all feeling.

Charlie Kirk, and all faithful Christians bearing witness to the holiness of the Kingdom of God, the ‘kingdom of the Son of His love,’ push into the aforementioned unholy communion. The darkness and delusion are exposed by the light of Christ, the power of God. It is this reality, the ascended Christ reality, that buggers the whole darkness-project. When self-actualization driven by my darkened inward turned navel feelings is challenged all it can do is recoil in shrieking anger and despise. The devil himself, identified by Jesus, as the father of lies, as the author of murder, becomes instigated by the light-bearers, as they reflect the Light of Light in the face of Jesus Christ, and he attempts to mount a counter-assault on such faces. This counter was what Charlie Kirk experienced; indeed, instigated by the devil, and implemented by his minions within the multilayered kingdom of darkness. Within this more volatile, this more active aspect of his kingdom, within the evil age, these agents of darkness, ensnared in ways that they cannot even imagine themselves, lash out. In this instance, Charlie Kirk experienced what, I’m sure, the Dragon of old, in all his futility, hoped would extinguish the penetration of the Kingdom of Light of Light, into his kingdom of darkness; particularly among the young. And yet because of the Great Reversal, the one where Jesus triumphed on the cross, making a public spectacle of the Enemy and his minions, has been flipped on its ugly dragon head. The seed of the Kerygma, the Gospel, the Power of God, has now been blown a thousandfold all across the globe. The Kingdom of Light of Light spreads, not by might, nor by power, but by the Spirit of the LORD. Like a massive dandelion, the breath of the Holy Spirit blows forth, in what appears to be dead seeds, only to spread God’s Word all across the lands. Indeed, so much so, that it penetrates the conclaves of darkness the Enemy has so ghoulishly and carefully been cultivating for his own murderous and destructive ends.

The bottom line, the eschatological reality, is that God has already won. Charlie Kirk’s death within the economy of God’s Kingdom is no death at all. Instead, it is a spur that only magnifies the strength and Light of God’s Kingdom; resulting in more seeing, rather than less. We grieve at Charlie’s death, and we really do!, but we know the Victory has been already had. Charlie stepped into the eternal arms of the everlasting Father the split-second that bullet ended his earthly life; at least “ended” for the time being. Charlie was in union with Christ. Christ has already died, been buried, rose again, and ascended for over two thousand years; thus, Charlie, and all the saints past, present, and future (as the Lord tarries) lives, not dies.

text:
Such a critic may, in fact, care more profoundly about its credibility and future than those who offer nothing but praise.

A national institution does not fear inquiry, because it understands that truth strengthens its foundations. Only fragile and compromised arrangements perceive questions as existential threats. If monarchy is to become a genuinely national institution, it must draw vitality from criticism rather than banish critics from the circle of patriotism.

Rereading the Metaphor of Chess

The metaphor of political chess remains useful only so long as it illuminates the strategic complexity of politics. In a constitutional monarchy, citizens are not pawns; advisers are not disposable pieces; and the monarch is not a player standing above the law.

In chess, the king must be preserved at almost any cost. Under constitutional government, however, what must ultimately be preserved is the lawful order, the country’s territorial integrity, the liberty of its citizens, and the sovereign right of the nation to determine its future.

If the preservation of a political personality—whether monarch, prince, or transitional leader—requires the sacrifice of these principles, then the metaphor has been inverted at its foundation. The individual exists to serve the institution; the institution does not exist to confer immunity upon the individual.

The master strategist is not the one who exploits every weakness until all opponents are destroyed. Political wisdom consists in preventing excitement, flattery, foreign influence, or personal ambition from overturning the entire Iranian board.

True victory is not the elimination of a rival. It is the establishment of an order in which no person—not even the most beloved figure in the country—may act without law, supervision, and responsibility.

Politics, unlike chess, is not won by annihilating half the society. The Iran of tomorrow will require the cooperation of people who disagree today. The language of transition must therefore preserve the possibility of coexistence after transition. Every word that denies a political rival’s humanity, Iranian identity, or right to speak becomes another stone in the foundations of a future despotism.

The Practical Architecture of the Third Feather

If the “The Simurgh's Third  Feather” is to rise above the level of metaphor, it must assume the form of clear and measurable actions:

A charter of public responsibility: Fundamental principles—including territorial integrity, national sovereignty, secular government, human rights, free elections, and the rejection of secret concessions to foreign powers—should be stated explicitly.

A professional advisory council: Members should be selected according to expertise, experience, independence of judgement, ethical standing, and diversity of perspective—not merely personal loyalty, media visibility, or private proximity.

Clearly defined authority: The public should know who is an official adviser, which matters fall within that person’s remit, and where the limits of that authority lie.

Financial transparency and disclosure of conflicts of interest: The sources of political funding, institutional support, and professional relationships capable of influencing decisions should be reported within a clear and lawful framework.

Rules governing foreign engagement: Foreign meetings and cooperation should proceed according to defined agendas, limited mandates, and appropriate reporting requirements, without disregarding the legitimate need for diplomatic confidentiality.

A mechanism for criticism and complaint: Citizens, specialists, and critics should be able to raise questions and objections without fear of intimidation or character assassination—and should receive reasoned, evidence-based answers.

Fixed terms for advisers: No one should become a permanent and irremovable member of an inner circle. Periodic evaluation, rotation of responsibility, and the possibility of dismissal are indispensable to

text:
𝗧𝗛𝗨𝗥𝗦𝗗𝗔𝗬 𝗢𝗙 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗧𝗪𝗘𝗡𝗧𝗬-𝗧𝗛𝗜𝗥𝗗 𝗪𝗘𝗘𝗞 𝗜𝗡 𝗢𝗥𝗗𝗜𝗡𝗔𝗥𝗬 𝗧𝗜𝗠𝗘
Thursday, September 10, 2026

1 Corinthians 8:1-7, 11-13
Psalm 139:1-3, 13-14, 23-24
Luke 6:27-38

𝗙𝗜𝗥𝗦𝗧 𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗗𝗜𝗡𝗚
1 Corinthians 8:1-7, 11-13

𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗲𝘅𝘁 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗦𝗲𝘁𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴

Corinthian Christians faced a practical question created by pagan society: could they eat meat associated with idol sacrifices? Some correctly understood that idols possess no true divinity, but Paul sees a deeper issue. Knowledge can be true yet used without charity. We should watch how the argument moves from knowledge, to the one true God, to conscience, then to scandal and self-denial. The governing principle is that 𝗖𝗵𝗿𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗮𝗻 𝗳𝗿𝗲𝗲𝗱𝗼𝗺 𝗶𝘀 𝗼𝗿𝗱𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗱 𝗯𝘆 𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗶𝘁𝘆. A lawful act must never be valued above the spiritual good of a brother for whom Christ died.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟭

Now concerning food offered to idols: we know that “all of us possess knowledge.” “Knowledge” puffs up, but love builds up.

Knowledge is good because truth perfects the intellect, but knowledge becomes disordered when pride turns it toward self-exaltation. Charity is higher because it orders the believer toward God and therefore toward the neighbor’s true good. The Corinthians know something correct, yet are failing to use it rightly. 𝗧𝗿𝘂𝘁𝗵 𝗺𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝗯𝗲 𝗴𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗻𝗲𝗱 𝗯𝘆 𝗹𝗼𝘃𝗲. Otherwise knowledge can become a weapon of superiority rather than an instrument of edification.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟮

If any one imagines that he knows something, he does not yet know as he ought to know.

Paul does not condemn certainty or learning. He condemns conceit. A person may possess a true conclusion yet fail to grasp its proper relation to humility, charity, and the good of others. Pride distorts genuine excellence by making the knower rest in himself. 𝗧𝗼 𝗸𝗻𝗼𝘄 “𝗮𝘀 𝗼𝗻𝗲 𝗼𝘂𝗴𝗵𝘁” means not merely possessing truth, but possessing it rightly, under wisdom and charity, without despising those whose understanding is weaker.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟯

But if one loves God, one is known by him.

God does not begin knowing a person when that person begins loving Him. Divine knowledge is eternal and perfect. The verse instead expresses belonging, favor, and friendship with God. Even our charity is first made possible by divine grace. Paul therefore turns attention away from boasting in what “I know” toward the God who first knows, calls, and loves. 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗴𝗹𝗼𝗿𝘆 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗖𝗵𝗿𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗮𝗻 𝗶𝘀 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗶𝗻 𝗵𝗶𝘀 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗹𝗹𝗲𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗮𝗹 𝘀𝘂𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗼𝗿𝗶𝘁𝘆, 𝗯𝘂𝘁 𝗶𝗻 𝗹𝗶𝘃𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗶𝗻 𝗚𝗼𝗱’𝘀 𝗹𝗼𝘃𝗲.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟰

Hence, as to the eating of food offered to idols, we know that “an idol has no real existence,” and that “there is no God but one.”

The material idol exists, but the supposed divinity attributed to it does not. Idolatry gives worship owed uniquely to God to something created. Paul therefore rejects both pagan worship and superstitious fear. A statue, spirit, ruler, or created power never crosses the infinite divide between Creator and creature. 𝗢𝗻𝗹𝘆 𝗚𝗼𝗱 𝗶𝘀 𝗚𝗼𝗱 𝗯𝘆 𝗻𝗮𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲. Everything else exists by participation, dependence, and divine causality.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟱

For although there may be so-called gods in heaven or on earth—as indeed there are many “gods” and many “lords”—

The ancient world called stars, spirits, rulers, and other beings “gods” and “lords.” Paul acknowledges the titles people use without conceding their truth. No created excellence, however great, possesses divinity by essence. 𝗧𝗵𝗲 “𝗺𝗮𝗻𝘆 𝗴𝗼𝗱𝘀” 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗴𝗼𝗱𝘀 𝗼𝗻𝗹𝘆 𝗯𝘆 𝗳𝗮𝗹𝘀𝗲 𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗯𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻. Christian monotheism is therefore not preference for one deity among many, but confession that only one divine nature exists.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟲

yet for us there is one God, the Father, from whom are all things and for whom we exist, and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things and through whom we exist.

“One God” does not exclude the Son from divinity, nor does “one Lord” exclude the Father from lordship. Father and Son are distinct Persons sharing one undivided divine essence. Since all things are “through” Christ, He cannot belong to the class of creatures. Creation itself comes through Him. 𝗣𝗮𝘂𝗹’𝘀 𝗺𝗼𝗻𝗼𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗶𝘀𝗺 𝗶𝘀 𝗧𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗶𝘁𝗮𝗿𝗶𝗮𝗻: from the Father, through the Son, all things exist and are ordered back to God.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟳

However, not all possess this knowledge. But some, through being hitherto accustomed to idols, eat food as really offered to an idol; and their conscience, being weak, is defiled.

Conscience applies moral knowledge to a concrete act. It may be mistaken and therefore needs formation, yet a person must not deliberately act against what he presently judges to be sinful. Converts long accustomed to pagan worship could still connect this food with idolatry. 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘀𝗰𝗶𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗱𝗼𝗲𝘀 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗰𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗺𝗼𝗿𝗮𝗹 𝘁𝗿𝘂𝘁𝗵, 𝗯𝘂𝘁 𝗶𝘁 𝗺𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝗯𝗲 𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝗲𝗱 𝗽𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗹𝘆 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝘃𝗶𝗼𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗱.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟭𝟭

And so by your knowledge this weak man is destroyed, the brother for whom Christ died.

Scandal is not merely upsetting someone. It is conduct that occasions another’s spiritual fall. Paul deliberately heightens the seriousness: the endangered person is weak, he is a brother, and Christ died for him. A trivial liberty is being weighed against a soul. 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝗽𝗶𝗿𝗶𝘁𝘂𝗮𝗹 𝗴𝗼𝗼𝗱 𝗼𝗳 𝗮 𝗯𝗿𝗼𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿 𝗶𝘀 𝗴𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝗻 𝗮 𝘁𝗲𝗺𝗽𝗼𝗿𝗮𝗹 𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁. Charity therefore measures freedom by whether its exercise helps or endangers another’s perseverance.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟭𝟮

Thus, sinning against your brethren and wounding their conscience when it is weak, you sin against Christ.

The brother’s spiritual injury reaches Christ because the believer belongs to Him. Charity loves the neighbor in God, so deliberately damaging the neighbor’s spiritual welfare is ultimately an offense against Christ Himself. This is the ecclesial depth of scandal. 𝗡𝗼 𝗖𝗵𝗿𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗮𝗻 𝗶𝘀 𝗮 𝘀𝗽𝗶𝗿𝗶𝘁𝘂𝗮𝗹 𝗶𝘀𝗹𝗮𝗻𝗱. Our conduct affects members of the same Body, and Christ takes seriously what is done to those joined to Him.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟭𝟯

Therefore, if food is a cause of my brother’s falling, I will never eat meat, lest I cause my brother to fall.

A lawful temporal good may be surrendered when its unnecessary exercise becomes a genuine occasion of another’s fall. Paul does not abandon truth or moral duty. He gives up food. The hierarchy matters. 𝗖𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗱𝗼𝗲𝘀 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗱𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗼𝘆 𝗳𝗿𝗲𝗲𝗱𝗼𝗺; 𝗶𝘁 𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗲𝗰𝘁𝘀 𝗶𝘁. True freedom includes the power to renounce what is lesser when the eternal good of another person is at stake.

𝗥𝗘𝗦𝗣𝗢𝗡𝗦𝗢𝗥𝗜𝗔𝗟 𝗣𝗦𝗔𝗟𝗠
Psalm 139:1-3, 13-14, 23-24

𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗲𝘅𝘁 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗦𝗲𝘁𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴

The Psalm contemplates what it means to be completely known by God. It begins with His knowledge of actions and thoughts, moves inward to His possession and formation of the hidden person, and ends with voluntary surrender to divine judgment and guidance. God knows creatures not by learning from them, but because He is their Creator and cause. Watch especially how the Psalm moves from “You know me” to “Search me” and finally “Lead me.” The believer no longer tries to escape divine knowledge but welcomes it, because the God who knows the heart is also the God who can lead it into Christ, the everlasting Way.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟭

O LORD, thou hast searched me and known me!

God does not discover facts through investigation. His knowledge is perfect and prior to our own because our very being depends upon His creative wisdom. Nothing interior is hidden from Him. 𝗚𝗼𝗱 𝗸𝗻𝗼𝘄𝘀 𝘂𝘀 𝗺𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝗱𝗲𝗲𝗽𝗹𝘆 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝗻 𝘄𝗲 𝗸𝗻𝗼𝘄 𝗼𝘂𝗿𝘀𝗲𝗹𝘃𝗲𝘀. This is both judgment and consolation: sin cannot hide, but neither can repentance, woundedness, or the desire to return.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟮

Thou knowest when I sit down and when I rise up; thou discernest my thoughts from afar.

God eternally knows free and contingent acts without making them involuntary. Sitting can signify humility and penitence; rising points toward restoration and resurrection. “From afar” recalls the sinner in the far country who is already known before completing his return. 𝗗𝗶𝘃𝗶𝗻𝗲 𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗸𝗻𝗼𝘄𝗹𝗲𝗱𝗴𝗲 𝗱𝗼𝗲𝘀 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗽𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲. God knows the free movement by which grace draws the sinner home.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟯

Thou searchest out my path and my lying down, and art acquainted with all my ways.

Providence embraces even particular human choices without removing freedom or responsibility. A sinner may choose his own road and experience its bitterness, yet he never passes outside God’s knowledge. God can permit the misery of wandering to become medicinal, awakening the desire to return. 𝗪𝗲 𝗺𝗮𝘆 𝗱𝗲𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝗚𝗼𝗱’𝘀 𝘄𝗮𝘆, 𝗯𝘂𝘁 𝘄𝗲 𝗻𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗿 𝗱𝗲𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝗚𝗼𝗱’𝘀 𝗸𝗻𝗼𝘄𝗹𝗲𝗱𝗴𝗲.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟭𝟯

For thou didst form my inward parts, thou didst knit me together in my mother’s womb.

The verse reaches from God’s knowledge into His creative lordship. The human person is not self-originating. His hidden life, inward powers, and very existence depend upon God as first cause. The ancient reading of the “reins” also points to the deepest desires and delights of the soul. 𝗚𝗼𝗱 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗼𝗻𝗹𝘆 𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗽𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗼𝗻; 𝗛𝗲 𝘀𝗲𝗲𝗸𝘀 𝘁𝗼 𝗿𝗲𝗼𝗿𝗱𝗲𝗿 𝘄𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗽𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗼𝗻 𝗹𝗼𝘃𝗲𝘀 toward Himself.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟭𝟰

I praise thee, for thou art fearful and wonderful. Wonderful are thy works! Thou knowest me right well;

Created goodness reflects divine wisdom according to the creature’s finite capacity. Wonder at human nature therefore should not terminate in self-exaltation but rise toward praise of the Creator. 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝘄𝗼𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿 𝗼𝗳 𝗺𝗮𝗻 𝗶𝘀 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗹 𝗯𝗲𝗰𝗮𝘂𝘀𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸 𝗼𝗳 𝗚𝗼𝗱 𝗶𝘀 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝘄𝗼𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿𝗳𝘂𝗹. True self-knowledge therefore matures into gratitude rather than self-worship.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟮𝟯

Search me, O God, and know my heart! Try me and know my thoughts!

God already knows the heart, so this prayer does not give Him new information. It is a surrender to the One whose judgment reaches deeper than human accusation. He alone knows whether the heart consents to evil or resists it. 𝗧𝗼 𝗮𝘀𝗸 𝗚𝗼𝗱 𝘁𝗼 “𝘀𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗰𝗵” 𝘂𝘀 𝗶𝘀 𝘁𝗼 𝘄𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗴𝗹𝘆 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗶𝗻 𝗛𝗶𝘀 𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁, trusting divine truth over both self-deception and false human judgment.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟮𝟰

And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting!

The everlasting Way is ultimately Christ Himself: “I am the Way, and the Truth, and the Life.” Our own paths can contain sin and end in death; Christ is the sinless Way leading to life. Yet man cannot attain supernatural beatitude by unaided nature. 𝗚𝗿𝗮𝗰𝗲 𝗱𝗼𝗲𝘀 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗺𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗹𝘆 𝘀𝗵𝗼𝘄 𝘂𝘀 𝗖𝗵𝗿𝗶𝘀𝘁. 𝗜𝘁 𝗵𝗲𝗮𝗹𝘀 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗺𝗼𝘃𝗲𝘀 𝘂𝘀 𝘀𝗼 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘄𝗲 𝗰𝗮𝗻 𝗳𝗿𝗲𝗲𝗹𝘆 𝗳𝗼𝗹𝗹𝗼𝘄 𝗛𝗶𝗺.

𝗚𝗢𝗦𝗣𝗘𝗟
Luke 6:27-38

𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗲𝘅𝘁 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗦𝗲𝘁𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴

Jesus has just called blessed those who suffer poverty, hatred, exclusion, and persecution. He now teaches how persecuted disciples must treat those responsible for their suffering. Watch the progression: love becomes beneficence, blessing, prayer, patience, generosity, and mercy. Christ then distinguishes supernatural charity from ordinary reciprocity and sets the Father Himself as the pattern. The passage ends with judgment, forgiveness, giving, and reward. 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗰𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗹 𝗽𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗰𝗶𝗽𝗹𝗲 𝗶𝘀 𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗶𝘁𝘆: the enemy is not loved for his evil, but as a person created by God and still capable of beatitude.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟮𝟳

“But I say to you that hear, Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,

Enemies are not loved as enemies, meaning for the evil by which they oppose us, but as human persons created by God and capable of salvation. Christ therefore demands more than refraining from hatred. He commands positive good. 𝗖𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗹𝗼𝘃𝗲𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗽𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗼𝗻 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗹𝗼𝘃𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝗶𝗻. Enemy-love does not abolish truth or justice; it refuses to desire the sinner’s evil.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟮𝟴

bless those who curse you, pray for those who abuse you.

Charity seeks the neighbor’s highest good, ultimately communion with God. Prayer for an enemy therefore seeks conversion, healing, and salvation rather than vengeance. This does not forbid prayer for justice, protection, or the defeat of evil. It forbids hatred from becoming the form of prayer. 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗖𝗵𝗿𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗮𝗻 𝗮𝘀𝗸𝘀 𝗚𝗼𝗱 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗲𝘃𝗶𝗹 𝗽𝗿𝗲𝘃𝗮𝗶𝗹, 𝗯𝘂𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗲𝘃𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗼𝗲𝗿 𝗯𝗲 𝗵𝗲𝗮𝗹𝗲𝗱.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟮𝟵

To him who strikes you on the cheek, offer the other also; and from him who takes away your cloak do not withhold your coat as well.

Patience does not mean approval of injustice. Charity may require correction of the wrongdoer or restraint of further harm. Christ forms the interior disposition that would rather suffer personal wrong than answer evil with vindictive hatred. 𝗧𝗵𝗲 “𝗼𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿 𝗰𝗵𝗲𝗲𝗸” 𝗶𝘀 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗮 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗼 𝗳𝗮𝗰𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗮𝗯𝘂𝘀𝗲. It is a command not to let another’s sin make vengeance master of our own heart.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟯𝟬

Give to every one who begs from you; and of him who takes away your goods do not ask them again.

Almsgiving is an act of charity through mercy. Because charity seeks genuine good, generosity must be prudent rather than indiscriminate. Yet prudence cannot become an excuse for hardness of heart. Created possessions are entrusted goods, not absolute possessions detached from the needs of others. 𝗠𝗲𝗿𝗰𝘆 𝗴𝗶𝘃𝗲𝘀 𝗯𝗲𝗰𝗮𝘂𝘀𝗲 𝗮𝗻𝗼𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿’𝘀 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗹 𝗻𝗲𝗲𝗱 𝗺𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘀 𝗯𝗲𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝗚𝗼𝗱.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟯𝟭

And as you wish that men would do to you, do so to them.

The Golden Rule presupposes rightly ordered desire. Whatever we happen to want does not automatically become morally good. Rather, we recognize that we rightly desire justice, patience, mercy, assistance, and truth from others. Christ turns that recognition outward. 𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗜 𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁𝗹𝘆 𝗱𝗲𝘀𝗶𝗿𝗲 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗺𝘆𝘀𝗲𝗹𝗳 𝗯𝗲𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗲𝘀 𝗮 𝗺𝗲𝗮𝘀𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗴𝗼𝗼𝗱 𝗜 𝗮𝗺 𝗼𝗯𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗲𝗱 𝘁𝗼 𝘀𝗲𝗲𝗸 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗮𝗻𝗼𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟯𝟮

“If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners love those who love them.

Natural affection and reciprocal friendship can be good, but they do not yet reveal the full supernatural power of charity. Love of an enemy especially manifests God as the reason for love because ordinary reciprocity has disappeared. 𝗚𝗿𝗮𝗰𝗲 𝗰𝗮𝗿𝗿𝗶𝗲𝘀 𝗹𝗼𝘃𝗲 𝗯𝗲𝘆𝗼𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗰𝗶𝗿𝗰𝗹𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘀𝗲 𝘄𝗵𝗼 𝗺𝗮𝗸𝗲 𝗹𝗼𝘃𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗺 𝗲𝗮𝘀𝘆. That is what reveals charity’s supernatural source.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟯𝟯

And if you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners do the same.

Beneficence is charity expressed in outward action. Reciprocal kindness is genuinely good, but Christ asks whether our goodness depends entirely upon receiving goodness first. Supernatural charity seeks another’s good because that person is loved in God. 𝗖𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗰𝗮𝗻 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗻𝘂𝗲 𝗱𝗼𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗴𝗼𝗼𝗱 𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗻 𝘄𝗵𝗲𝗻 𝗴𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝘁𝘂𝗱𝗲 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗶𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗰𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗱𝗶𝘀𝗮𝗽𝗽𝗲𝗮𝗿.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟯𝟰

And if you lend to those from whom you hope to receive, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, to receive as much again.

Christ does not abolish justice in lawful debts or contracts. He exposes a generosity controlled entirely by self-interest. Mercy can respond to another’s need even when repayment is uncertain or impossible. 𝗖𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗯𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗸𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗵𝗲𝗮𝗿𝘁’𝘀 𝗯𝗼𝗻𝗱𝗮𝗴𝗲 𝘁𝗼 “𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘄𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝗜 𝗴𝗲𝘁 𝗯𝗮𝗰𝗸?” and asks instead what real good can be done for the person before us.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟯𝟱

But love your enemies, and do good, and lend, expecting nothing in return; and your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High; for he is kind to the ungrateful and the selfish.

Enemy-love especially reveals God as charity’s motive. “Sons of the Most High” signifies likeness to the Father’s goodness. The promised reward does not mean unaided works purchase eternal life. Eternal life exceeds natural human power, yet works proceeding from grace and charity truly receive the reward God graciously promises. 𝗚𝗼𝗱 𝗰𝗿𝗼𝘄𝗻𝘀 𝗛𝗶𝘀 𝗼𝘄𝗻 𝗴𝗿𝗮𝗰𝗲 𝗮𝘁 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸 𝗶𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗳𝗿𝗲𝗲𝗹𝘆 𝗰𝗼𝗼𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗯𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗿.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟯𝟲

Be merciful, even as your Father is merciful.

Mercy is compassion for another’s misery joined to the desire to relieve it. The Father Himself is the exemplar. We cannot equal infinite divine mercy in degree, yet grace creates a real likeness to it in us. 𝗖𝗵𝗿𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗮𝗻 𝗺𝗲𝗿𝗰𝘆 𝗶𝘀 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝘀𝗼𝗳𝘁𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘀 𝘁𝗼𝘄𝗮𝗿𝗱 𝗲𝘃𝗶𝗹. Because sin itself is misery, true mercy seeks healing, conversion, forgiveness, and restoration.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟯𝟳

“Judge not, and you will not be judged; condemn not, and you will not be condemned; forgive, and you will be forgiven;

Christ does not forbid all judgment, because justice requires truthful moral discernment. Judgment becomes sinful when it is rash, exceeds our authority, lacks sufficient grounds, or proceeds from an unjust disposition. Forgiveness likewise excludes vindictive hatred. 𝗝𝗲𝘀𝘂𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗯𝗶𝗱𝘀 𝗿𝗮𝘀𝗵 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗺𝗲𝗿𝗰𝗶𝗹𝗲𝘀𝘀 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗺𝗻𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻, 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁𝗳𝘂𝗹 𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗼𝗴𝗻𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗼𝗳 𝗴𝗼𝗼𝗱 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗲𝘃𝗶𝗹.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝟯𝟴

give, and it will be given to you; good measure, pressed down, shaken together, running over, will be put into your lap. For the measure you give will be the measure you get back.”

The promise rejects both self-salvation and the denial that grace-filled works truly matter. Eternal life cannot be earned by unaided nature, but works proceeding from grace and charity truly merit according to God’s gracious ordering. 𝗚𝗿𝗮𝗰𝗲 𝗱𝗼𝗲𝘀 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗺𝗮𝗸𝗲 𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗱𝗲𝗲𝗱𝘀 𝗶𝗿𝗿𝗲𝗹𝗲𝘃𝗮𝗻𝘁. It makes genuinely meritorious acts of mercy possible, and Christ promises that the Father will not forget them.

𝗦𝘂𝗺𝗺𝗮𝗿𝘆 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗘𝘅𝗵𝗼𝗿𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

Today’s readings converge on one great truth: 𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗹𝗶𝗳𝗲 𝗯𝗲𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝗚𝗼𝗱 𝗶𝘀 𝗺𝗲𝗮𝘀𝘂𝗿𝗲𝗱 𝗯𝘆 𝘁𝗿𝘂𝘁𝗵 𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝗲𝗱 𝗯𝘆 𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗶𝘁𝘆. Paul shows that correct knowledge is not enough if our freedom damages a weaker brother. The Psalm shows why nothing in us is hidden from God, who knows our thoughts, forms our life, examines our ways, and calls us into Christ, the everlasting Way. Jesus then reveals the positive form of holiness: love enemies, do good, pray, give, forgive, show mercy, judge justly, and expect the reward God promises to works born of grace.

The thread joining them is conversion from self-reference to God-reference. Knowledge is no longer about proving ourselves right. Possessions are no longer absolute. Freedom is no longer mere permission. Judgment is no longer self-exaltation. Even love is no longer restricted to those who return it. 𝗚𝗿𝗮𝗰𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗼𝗿𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀 𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘆𝘁𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗼𝘄𝗮𝗿𝗱 𝗚𝗼𝗱 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗲 𝗴𝗼𝗼𝗱 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗻𝗲𝗶𝗴𝗵𝗯𝗼𝗿.

So examine what your freedom does to others. Let God search the hidden motives beneath your actions. Refuse vengeance without surrendering truth. Give without making repayment the measure of mercy. Forgive because you need forgiveness. Love even where love is not returned. And above all, ask to be led in the everlasting Way. 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗖𝗵𝗿𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗮𝗻 𝗹𝗶𝗳𝗲 𝗶𝘀 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗺𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗹𝘆 𝗸𝗻𝗼𝘄𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘄𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗶𝘀 𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁. 𝗜𝘁 𝗶𝘀 𝗯𝗲𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘀𝗼 𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗻𝘀𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝗲𝗱 𝗯𝘆 𝗴𝗿𝗮𝗰𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘄𝗲 𝗯𝗲𝗴𝗶𝗻 𝘁𝗼 𝗹𝗼𝘃𝗲, 𝗷𝘂𝗱𝗴𝗲, 𝗴𝗶𝘃𝗲, 𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗴𝗶𝘃𝗲, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘀𝗵𝗼𝘄 𝗺𝗲𝗿𝗰𝘆 𝗮𝘀 𝗰𝗵𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗿𝗲𝗻 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗙𝗮𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿.

text:
An incisive piece by @leelajacinto for France 24 on the BAPS temple in Robbinsville, New Jersey, and a difficult one to read.

A stone carver from Rajasthan, his passport taken on arrival. A colleague, Mohan Lal, who asked to be taken to a hospital and was kept in a trailer until he died. More than a hundred men freed by an FBI raid in 2021, most of them Dalit, most classified by BAPS as religious volunteers, most paid around a dollar an hour. Last year the DOJ closed the criminal investigation without charges and without explanation.

@SunitaSunitaV of Hindus for Human Rights puts it rightly: a case dismissed is not a case answered. No apology has ever been offered to these men. And the class action has not gone away. The civil wage-theft claim remains intact and is moving forward.

Shocking that these allegations were not considered while deciding whether the Indian government should play an active role in the inauguration of this new BAPS  temple in France.

TRON Is Rethinking The Cost Of On-Chain Interaction

What if using a blockchain didn’t always begin with the question, “Do I have enough gas?”

That question is still one of the quietest sources of friction in Web3. A user may have the asset they want to use, yet still need another token simply to make the transaction happen.

TRON approaches this differently through a resource model built around Energy and Bandwidth, creating more flexible ways to support on-chain activity.

➠ Energy Turns Network Capacity Into Something Users Can Manage

Smart contract execution requires computational resources.

On TRON, Energy represents those resources.

Users can obtain Energy through TRX staking, effectively turning staked capital into access to network resources.

But that doesn't mean staking is the right answer for everyone.

An occasional user may not want to lock additional TRX just because they need to execute a few smart contract transactions.

That is where flexibility becomes important.

➠ JustLend Adds An On-Demand Option

JustLend DAO’s Energy Rental gives users another route to obtaining Energy without requiring them to stake additional TRX specifically for that purpose.

This can be particularly useful when interacting with:

▫️DeFi protocols
▫️Token swaps
▫️Lending and borrowing platforms
▫️Smart contracts
▫️Other supported TRON applications

The interesting part is the change in mindset.

Instead of thinking, “How much capital do I need to lock?”

Users can also think, “How much resource do I actually need right now?”

That distinction can make network-resource management considerably more practical.

➠ GasFree Removes Another Piece Of Friction

Energy Rental and GasFree solve different problems.

Energy Rental helps users access Energy.

GasFree, where supported, can allow applications to sponsor eligible transaction fees so users don't necessarily need to acquire TRX just to pay for those transactions.

That can dramatically simplify the first interaction with a blockchain application.

The user doesn't have to understand the entire resource model before getting started.

They can simply focus on completing the action.

➠ One Network, Different Paths For Different Users

Blockchain users don't behave the same way.

A frequent DeFi trader may prefer maintaining resources through staking or renting Energy when necessary.

A developer may care about predictable access to resources during repeated contract interactions.

A newcomer may benefit most from a GasFree experience that removes the need to manage fees altogether.

Instead of forcing every participant into one approach, TRON’s resource ecosystem provides different mechanisms for different situations.

That is a powerful usability principle.

➠ The Best Fee Experience Might Be The One You Don't Notice

Users don't wake up wanting to manage blockchain resources.

They want to swap.

Lend.

Stake.

Pay.

Trade.

Interact.

The more infrastructure can handle the complexity underneath those actions, the closer Web3 gets to feeling like a normal digital service rather than a technical environment that users must learn before they can use it.

This is where resource design becomes more than a technical detail.

It becomes part of adoption.

➠ Making The Blockchain Easier To Use

Through Energy, staking, Energy Rental, and supported GasFree experiences, TRON offers multiple ways to approach the cost of on-chain activity.

No single mechanism has to serve every user.

And that may be the bigger advantage.

Because blockchain adoption won't come only from networks processing more transactions.

It will also come from making those transactions easier to understand, easier to access, and less disruptive to the user experience.

Less time thinking about gas.
More time using the application.

text:
"Facts are stubborn things; and whatever may be our wishes, our inclinations, or the dictates of our passion, they cannot alter the state of facts and evidence," -John Adams

She’s always pleaded not guilty. 
Facts and Massachusetts law below:

-The DA charged first-degree murder and stayed there. 

-A grand jury later indicted three first-degree murders. That proceeding is secret and one-sided: only the prosecution presents evidence. 

-After the grand jury indicted her, she pleaded not guilty. Massachusetts has no “I plead NGRI” box. You plead not guilty, then raise lack of criminal responsibility at trial.

-She stayed not guilty at trial and raised lack of criminal responsibility. That puts the burden on the Commonwealth: prove the crime and prove she was responsible.

-With the DA refusing to move off murder 1, LCR (lack of criminal responsibility) was the only workable route left to beat that charge.

-Reddington motioned to bifurcate: acts first, responsibility second.

-The judge denied the motion.

-Then Reddington offered a stipulation: we will not fight that her alleged actions caused the deaths if the case can focus on responsibility.

-That is not a guilty plea to murder. It is conceding alleged causation, not first-degree guilt.

-He asked for a Bowden instruction (bad police work can create reasonable doubt). Prosecutors objected. There is no clear public report that the judge gave the formal Bowden charge.

-Reddington could still argue the investigation was deficient, and he did so in the defense closing.

-Under the law, she never pleaded guilty and never formally admitted that she committed the act of murder. 

In the eyes of the law, Lindsay did not confess to the murders. The law does not treat “what she reported remembering” and “I am guilty of murder” as the same thing. They are treated differently because a crime is not just a physical event. Murder requires proof that she did the act and that the law can blame her for it. Once LCR was raised, that burden stayed on the Commonwealth.

text:
Did India turn down a seat at the UNSC?

In 1950, India’s ambassador to the US, Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit, told Nehru that Washington was considering giving India China’s UNSC seat.

Nehru replied that India would not take the seat “at the cost of China”, arguing that Beijing deserved UN representation.

In 1955, the Soviet Union also floated the idea of India joining the Security Council, but Nehru later told Parliament there had been no formal or informal offer.

These were informal proposals, not concrete offers of a permanent seat.

Somaliland and the MEAD Conference

WASHINGTON, D.C. -The MEAD Conference, held in Washington, D.C., has concluded following discussions involving senior leaders, policymakers, and experts from the United States, the Middle East, and Europe.

According to Mohamed Ali Bile, who was among those invited to attend, the conference provided an important platform for discussing political and security developments, as well as the future direction of the Middle East and the United States’ engagement with the region.

Somaliland was represented at the conference by President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi “Irro” and members of his delegation. According to Bile, Somaliland was the only African country invited to participate in the conference.

In addition to the main sessions, President Irro and members of his delegation took part in a number of important side meetings with political leaders, policymakers, and experts attending the conference. These engagements provided an opportunity to discuss issues of strategic importance to Somaliland and the wider region.

Bile highlighted Somaliland’s strategic geographical position, noting that it sits at the intersection of the Horn of Africa, the Red Sea, the Gulf, and the broader Middle East. Somaliland’s location along the Red Sea and near one of the world’s most important maritime trade routes gives it significant relevance to discussions surrounding regional security, trade, economic cooperation, and stability.

“Today, no country can address every challenge on its own,” Bile said, emphasizing the importance of international cooperation. He argued that countries with strategic interests in the Horn of Africa and the Red Sea can benefit from cooperation and engagement with Somaliland.

Beyond the substantive discussions at the conference, Bile said MEAD also offered Somaliland an important opportunity to establish relationships with influential leaders, policymakers, and experts from around the world.

He stressed that developing such relationships could help Somaliland advance its political interests and strengthen opportunities for international cooperation, particularly in the areas of diplomacy, security, and economic development.

For Somaliland, participation in international forums such as MEAD represents an opportunity to increase its visibility, strengthen diplomatic engagement, and highlight its strategic importance in the Horn of Africa and Red Sea region.

“Guul Somaliland.”

Mohamed Ali Bile

text:
🚨 TRUMP FLOATS $5,000 “DIVIDEND” FOR EVERY U.S. ADULT IF GOP WINS CONGRESS.

DALLAS, UNITED STATES - President Donald Trump used a primetime appearance at a Republican midterm convention to promise a $5,000 payment to every American adult if his party keeps control of both chambers of Congress. He framed the proposal as a “dividend” tied to what he described as strong economic performance, offering few details on how the plan would be funded or implemented.

The pledge came as Republicans try to energize voters ahead of November’s elections. Trump spoke for nearly two hours, casting the midterms as a personal referendum and urging supporters to “pretend I’m on the ballot.” His proposal would cost well over a trillion dollars, far exceeding current tariff revenues, which he has previously suggested could help finance similar ideas.

The announcement immediately raised questions about legality and feasibility. Any nationwide payout would require congressional approval, and the federal government is already running large annual deficits with national debt above 40 trillion dollars. Senior administration figures later hinted the payments might exclude wealthier Americans, though no formal plan has been released.

Trump has floated direct payments before, including smaller dividends tied to tariff collections and bonuses for service members. None approached the scale of the new proposal, which would involve distributing checks to more than 240 million adults. The idea arrives as Republicans confront historical midterm headwinds and polling that shows voter frustration with inflation and rising living costs.

The Dallas convention marks the party’s first attempt at a dedicated midterm gathering, with Trump scheduled to appear again alongside other senior figures. His promise dominated the event, overshadowing policy discussions and campaign strategy sessions. The last time Washington issued broad payments to households was during the pandemic, when Congress authorized several rounds of stimulus checks. Those programs totaled far less per person and were enacted during a national emergency.

Trump told attendees the payments would be called the “Trump Dividend.” He offered no timeline for when Americans might receive the money, leaving the proposal’s future tied entirely to the outcome of November’s vote.

text:
Rome did not lose provinces by accident.
It lost men. Sometimes thousands of them. Then it pretended they had never existed.That is the story of the Ninth.Legio IX Hispana. The Spanish Ninth. Caesar’s old sword. The machine that helped take Britain. Five thousand professionals in iron, plus the trail of slaves, mules, clerks and ghosts that always followed a Roman legion. For seventy years they were the northern fist of the empire on the island. Then, sometime after a stone was carved in York in the year 108, they fall out of history like a body dropped into a peat bog. No funeral. No triumph. No official lie polished enough to survive. Just absence.That absence is louder than most victories.The last thing the Ninth left us in Britain is not a battlefield. It is paperwork in stone. A gateway inscription at Eboracum — York — dated to Trajan’s titles in AD 108. The emperor’s names. The legion’s name. A gate built “by the agency of the Ninth Legion Hispana.” After that, Britain goes quiet on them. By 122 a different legion, VI Victrix, is sitting in their fortress. Hadrian himself has come to the island. A wall of stone begins to crawl across the throat of the north. And the Ninth is not on it. Not a tile. Not a dedication. Not a boast.Rome built monuments to units that died well. It also erased units that died badly. The Ninth got the second treatment.They had already almost died once. In 60 or 61, when Boudica burned the south, a detachment of the Ninth marched to stop her and was cut to pieces. Tacitus says the infantry was slaughtered; only the cavalry escaped. The legion was rebuilt, because Rome could still afford to rebuild then. They went north with Agricola. They survived a night assault in the dark around 82. They stood in the order of battle at Mons Graupius while the auxiliaries did the killing. They were not a glamorous legion. They were a work legion. Frontier dogs. The kind of unit an empire uses until the day the frontier bites back.Then the record snaps.There are four graves for the Ninth, and none of them has a body.The first grave is the one everyone wants. Scotland. Caledonia. A column marching beyond the last fort, into weather and heather and a people who had already learned that Romans bleed. One bad commander. One wrong valley. One morning when the mist does not lift and the screaming starts from three sides at once. Five thousand men do not vanish in a parade. They vanish when the ground itself becomes the enemy. This is the version that made novels and films, because it is the version that feels like fate. Hadrian’s Wall looks, in this telling, less like a border and more like a scar: the empire drawing a line after something unspeakable happened north of it.The second grave is closer to home. Not the Highlands. The province itself. Brigantes in revolt. A war in the north of what is now England around the start of Hadrian’s reign. The Historia Augusta hints at a British disaster serious enough to demand an imperial response. Tombstones of soldiers from other units talk about an expedition sent to put Britain back together. If the Ninth was the garrison of York, they would have been first into the fire. First in, last seen.The third grave is not Britain at all. Tiles and a bronze pendant stamped LEG HISP IX turned up at Nijmegen, on the Lower Rhine. Maybe the whole legion was transferred. Maybe only a detachment. The dating is a knife fight among specialists: some say those stamps can sit after 108, some say they belong earlier, some say they prove nothing except that a few Ninth men once baked bricks in the Netherlands. If the legion did leave Britain alive, the map of death moves east. Judea, 132–135. The Bar Kokhba revolt, a meat grinder that chewed through Roman units and spat out silence. Or Armenia and Parthia in the 160s, where another Roman army walked into a trap and did not walk out. The Ninth is missing from the big legion lists by the late second century. Something killed the name. The only argument is where.The fourth grave is the cruelest: disgrace. Not annihilation in battle, but deletion. A legion that broke, deserted, mutinied, or simply failed so publicly that Rome chose forgetting over mourning. Damnatio memoriae for five thousand men. In that version the Ninth did not die in the heather. They were unwritten. Here is what we actually know, stripped of cinema.The Ninth is last nailed to Britain in 108.
They are gone from York by 122.
They are gone from the official roster of the army by the 160s at latest.
There is no mass grave with their eagle.
There is no dispatch from a surviving tribune.
There is no Caledonian boast carved in stone that says we ate the Ninth.That is the entire cathedral of evidence. Everything else is inference standing on a cliff.And that is why the story will not die.Empires are supposed to be good at accounting. Rome counted wheat, counted ships, counted the exact number of lashes a man was owed. A legion was not a vibe. It was a serial number with a standard, a pay chest, a burial club, a paper trail that stretched from the Rhine to the desert. When that machine stops appearing, something violent has happened — either to the men, or to the memory of the men.The north of Britain was the perfect place for that violence. It was wet, tribal, unfinished. Rome never fully digested it. Agricola won battles and still had to leave. Later emperors built walls instead of finishing the job. A wall is an admission. It says: we can hold this line, but we cannot hold what lies beyond it. If you want a myth with a spine, that is the spine. The Ninth marches into the part of the map Rome could not civilize, and the map closes over them. Do not confuse the myth with a verdict. Serious archaeologists will tell you, correctly, that we have not found the wreckage. No carpet of lorica plates in a Scottish glen. No eagle in a peat cutting. Absence of evidence is not a battlefield. The Rhine tiles are real. Later careers of some officers associated with the Ninth are real. The honest sentence is ugly and short: the Ninth disappeared from the record in the early second century, and Britain is only the most famous place it could have died.But history is not only what can be footnoted. History is also what a civilization cannot stand to leave unexplained.Rome could survive losing a battle. It had lost battles before. What it could not survive, in its own mind, was the idea that the edge of the world could swallow a legion whole and offer no receipt. So later ages did the work Rome refused. They wrote the receipt themselves. A novel in 1954. Films. Documentaries that keep walking the same rain-soaked ridges. Every generation puts the Ninth back on the road north, because a clean disappearance is more frightening than a listed defeat.Five thousand men.
One last gate in York.
Then weather.If they died in Britain, they died at the limit of the system that made them. If they died in Judea or Armenia, they died as spare parts shipped to the next fire. If they were erased, they died twice. The heather version remains the one that sticks because it has the right shape: the most organized army on earth walking off the paved road and into a country that did not recognize roads as power.Stand on Hadrian’s Wall on a bad day and the theory stops being academic. Wind comes off the north like an argument. The stone looks less like architecture and more like a locked door. Behind you, the empire. Ahead of you, the blank.That blank still has a name.The Ninth.They were not lost because they were weak.
They were lost because the world at the edge of Rome was allowed to stay wild long enough to take something Rome thought was permanent.And two thousand years later we are still looking for the bones, which means the legion is doing the one thing a Roman unit was never supposed to do. It is still marching.
Just not on any map we own.

text:
🚨For almost 10 years, the most wanted terrorist in the world vanished.

Governments searched. Intelligence agencies followed countless leads. A $25 million reward was offered for information leading to his capture.

Yet Osama bin Laden remained hidden.

Then one small clue changed everything.

Bin Laden was the founder of al-Qaeda, the terrorist organization responsible for the September 11, 2001 attacks in the United States, which killed nearly 3,000 people.

After the attacks, the United States launched an enormous international manhunt.

Many believed bin Laden was hiding somewhere in the remote mountains along the Afghanistan-Pakistan border.

Years passed without finding him.

But U.S. intelligence officers were quietly working on another approach.

Instead of searching directly for bin Laden, they began trying to identify the people carrying messages for him.

One courier became particularly important.

After years of intelligence work, investigators eventually tracked the courier to an unusual compound in Abbottabad, Pakistan.

And this wasn’t some isolated cave in the mountains.

The compound was in a populated city, not far from Pakistan’s military academy.

Its security immediately raised suspicions.

High walls surrounded the property. Privacy was unusually strict. The residents reportedly had no normal telephone or internet connection, and garbage was burned rather than simply collected.

Then intelligence analysts noticed something else.

A tall man regularly walked around inside the compound’s courtyard.

Because cameras couldn’t clearly identify him, analysts reportedly referred to him as “the Pacer.”

They suspected the mystery man might be bin Laden.

But they couldn’t prove it.

There was no photograph confirming his identity and no certainty that he was actually inside.

President Barack Obama therefore faced an extraordinary decision:

Raid the compound based on intelligence that could still be wrong—or wait and risk losing the target.

Obama authorized the operation.

On the night of May 1–2, 2011, U.S. Navy SEALs flew secretly into Abbottabad aboard helicopters.

Then something went wrong.

One helicopter made a hard landing inside the compound.

The mission continued anyway.

The SEALs entered the buildings and moved through the compound.

On the upper floor of the main house, they found Osama bin Laden.

He was killed during the raid.

The team collected computers, documents and other material before leaving. The damaged helicopter was destroyed so sensitive technology wouldn’t be left behind.

The operation took roughly 40 minutes.

Hours later, President Obama appeared on television and announced:

The United States had conducted an operation that killed Osama bin Laden.

Nearly a decade after 9/11, one of the longest and most consequential manhunts of the modern era was over.

And after years of speculation that he was hiding deep inside some remote cave…

The trail had ultimately led to a walled compound in a Pakistani city.

text:
Quinn Emanuel Hit by Breach Exposing Muddy Waters Files Amid Bitter Disqualification Battle https://t.co/iMkkUXVgyE
Litigation powerhouse Quinn Emanuel suffered a social engineering breach exposing confidential Muddy Waters files—exploding into a massive reputation clash just days before a federal disqualification.  

When a premier global litigation powerhouse becomes the victim of an elementary social engineering compromise, the legal fallout is brutal. When the exposed files happen to belong to the world's most aggressive short seller—with whom the law firm is locked in a bitter conflict-of-interest feud—it transforms into an outright public relations inferno.

On September 3, Reuters broke the news that top-tier trial firm Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan suffered a data breach after an unauthorized intruder gained access through social engineering. According to an August 25 disclosure letter sent directly to counsel for activist short-selling firm Muddy Waters, the attacker compromised a single internal user account on August 14, gaining unauthorized access to files stored inside an internal software platform. Among the compromised records: sensitive litigation documents involving Muddy Waters obtained during high-stakes Florida litigation.

The Intersection of Lawfare and Reputation Warfare
Under normal circumstances, corporate counsel would issue a quiet regulatory disclosure, offer credit monitoring, and pivot toward mitigation. But this was anything but normal.

At the very moment the breach became public, Muddy Waters and its founder, Carson Block, were already waging aggressive smear-campaign defense and legal warfare to disqualify Quinn Emanuel in a Texas federal court. Quinn Emanuel had been retained by Techtronic Industries (TTI) to prosecute a high-profile defamation and conspiracy lawsuit against Muddy Waters. The short seller forcefully objected, arguing Quinn had previously represented Carson Block and Muddy Waters during Department of Justice and SEC investigations into activist short selling, thereby acquiring sensitive trade secrets and internal investigative methods.

When news of the security breach surfaced, Muddy Waters bypassed standard corporate niceties and launched an immediate bad-press operation against Quinn Emanuel's brand equity. Muddy Waters fired off a blistering public broadside: "Just when we thought Quinn couldn't be more outrageous than eagerly representing new clients who want to sue old ones, we learned that Quinn failed to protect our sensitive information from social engineering hacking."

Within days, the Texas federal court handed down a stinging ruling disqualifying Quinn Emanuel from representing TTI, creating a devastating one-two punch to the law firm’s institutional reputation.

When Security Failures Become Strategic Ammo
For elite institutions and professional services firms, high-stakes disputes no longer stay confined to the courtroom docket. Legal conflicts regularly spill over into coordinated corporate reputation management battles.

When adversaries weaponize external missteps—such as operational breaches, ethics complaints, or regulatory notices—they dictate the public narrative across media, investor channels, and search engines. As search algorithms and LLM answer engines ingest news of conflicts of interest and data lapses, the brand narrative is quickly reframed around negligence rather than legal dominance.

Without proactive defense intelligence and an aggressive containment strategy, a single compromised identity can unravel years of courtroom prestige, leaving legacy brands scrambling under relentless crisis reputation management pressure.

How https://t.co/FsSTbGVTyn Would Respond

When a high-profile law firm or corporate target suffers an operational failure in the crosshairs of an adversarial dispute, silence and cookie-cutter regulatory statements guarantee reputational defeat. In the first 72 hours, Quinn Emanuel surrendered control of the narrative, allowing Carson Block and Muddy Waters to frame the breach as systemic incompetence and ethical negligence.

Here is how https://t.co/FsSTbGVTyn would have managed the response:

Preemptive Stakeholder Seeding (Hours 0–24): Before regulatory notifications inevitably leaked to legal reporters, we would execute an authoritative counter-publishing strategy across high-authority financial and legal trade publications. The incident should have been framed strictly as an isolated social-engineering phishing attempt mitigated by rapid internal containment protocols, insulating the broader firm from charges of systemic negligence.

AI & Search Engine Narrative Control (Hours 24–48): Adversaries weaponize major breaches to degrade a target's search presence. Through our ai-search-reputation-management and search suppression capabilities, we would ensure corporate search results and AI answer engines (Perplexity, ChatGPT Search, Google AI Overviews) emphasize containment and security resilience rather than conflict-of-interest allegations.

De-escalation & Legal PR Alignment (Hours 48–72): Instead of issuing a cold "no comment" to Muddy Waters' public mockery, we would deploy targeted crisis-reputation-management messaging separating the unrelated cyber incident from the active Texas disqualification motion, blunting the opponent's leverage before the presiding judge and prospective enterprise clients.
