text:
After the war, Britain offered land grants in Upper and Lower Canada to disbanded regular soldiers as a way to settle loyal, militarily useful men along potential invasion routes. Units that had served in the Chesapeake campaign, including the 44th Regiment of Foot (present at Bladensburg and Washington), were eligible. Some veterans of that regiment took up locations at the Perth Military Settlement in what is now eastern Ontario.

Not every veteran stayed; many abandoned their lots. Those who remained, and their descendants, became part of the population of British North America and, after Confederation, of Canada. They were British subjects throughout; formal Canadian citizenship as a distinct legal status came much later.

Similar to the events that took place when the Spirit of the Lord fell upon the Gentiles in Acts 10, and with the dedication of the Temple of Solomon, the Spirit of the Lord fell upon the congregation who was present for the dedication of the Kirtland Temple. 
At the Kirtland Temple dedication on 27 March 1836, Joseph Smith offered the revealed dedicatory prayer (now D&C 109) before a packed congregation that then gave the Hosanna Shout and sang “The Spirit of God Like a Fire Is Burning.” Participants described a Pentecost-like outpouring: a sound like a rushing mighty wind filled the house, many spoke in tongues and prophesied, and angels were seen—Frederick G. Williams testified that a heavenly personage entered during the opening prayer and sat in the pulpits, while that evening more than four hundred priesthood holders rose together as the temple appeared filled with angels and a pillar of fire was seen resting upon the building from outside. The manifestations continued in following meetings; a week later, on 3 April, the Savior appeared to Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery, accepted the house, and was followed by Moses, Elias, and Elijah, who committed keys of gathering, the gospel of Abraham, and sealing.
When Solomon dedicated the temple, the glory of the Lord filled the house in a visible, overwhelming way.
After the ark was placed in the Most Holy Place and the priests came out, a cloud filled the temple so that the priests could not stand to minister (1 Kings 8:10–11; 2 Chronicles 5:13–14). Chronicles notes that this happened as the singers and trumpeters praised the Lord with one voice: “For he is good; for his mercy endureth for ever.”
After Solomon’s dedicatory prayer, fire came down from heaven, consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and the glory of the Lord filled the house again; the priests could not enter, and the people bowed with their faces to the ground and worshiped (2 Chronicles 7:1–3).
These signs—the cloud of glory and the fire from heaven—were understood as God’s acceptance of the house, much as the cloud had filled the tabernacle in Moses’ day.
This pattern was again fulfilled with the Kirtland Temple, as evidence of the Lord's acceptance to the house dedicated to His Name.

text:
The Priest We Need

Since then we have a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus, the Son of God, let us hold fast our confession … Let us then with confidence draw near to the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy and find grace to help in time of need.
Hebrews 4:14-16

The Old Testament underlines again and again the weight of responsibility on high priests in Israel (see, for example, Exodus 29 and Leviticus 16). Being the high priest was not to be taken lightly. Only he could enter the Most Holy Place, the inner chamber of the Jewish temple. Only he could offer a blood sacrifice “for the unintentional sins of the people” (Hebrews 9:7). Although he was not without sin, he served as an advocate for his community before God.

But, as the writer of Hebrews shows us, there has been one Great High Priest—namely, Jesus—who did what no other priest could do and shouldered a responsibility the weight of which no other human could bear.

Jesus did not go through a curtain into the Most Holy Place in the Jerusalem temple. Instead, as God’s Son, He passed through the heavens, so that He now appears on our behalf before the Father’s throne. We need not lament His physical absence on earth, not only because He is present with us through the Holy Spirit but also because His absence means that even now He is directly speaking to God the Father on our behalf (Hebrews 7:25).

That is why in the New Testament, ministry is not set apart for an order of priests who make blood sacrifices. Those who are called by God and given both the privilege and responsibility of leading and teaching God’s people do not have to advocate before God for His people in the way Old Testament priests did. Because our Great High Priest has offered up the one great sacrifice for sins, there is no need for any other advocate. Indeed, His priesthood leaves room for no other offerings for sin, either in heaven or on earth. He alone could die for us and speak for us, and He alone has done it.

The very greatness of Christ’s priesthood lies in the fact that He has offered Himself for our sins once and for all. We need nothing more than to recognize that “he holds his priesthood permanently, because he continues forever” (Hebrews 7:24). Jesus alone is able to save those of us who come to God on the basis of His merits. He always lives to intercede for His people. He is doing so, right at this very moment, for you. So you can live confident of access to the heavenly throne room whenever you pray, and access for your soul on the day you die. Today, all you need to do is hold fast to your confession of faith in the Great High Priest, who has done all that is needed.

Alistair Begg

🔴 Trump pledges $5K payout to US adults if Republicans win midterms — so he can ‘finish the job’
By Steven Nelson
Published Sep. 9, 2026, 9:50 p.m. ET

1.3K Comments
Trump urges voters to let GOP ‘finish the job’ in midterm convention speech

DALLAS — President Trump headlined the Republican Party’s first-ever midterm convention Wednesday night, boasting about his record and offering every American $5,000 if Republicans hold control of Congress in the Nov. 3 election.

Trump implored listeners to “pretend that I’m on the ballot” so he can “finish the job” —presenting a stark choice between “radical left communists” and a continuation of his populist agenda. 

The president offered Americans a major financial incentive to stick with him in what he called the “best part” of his energetic barnstorming-style 107-minute speech.

Follow The Post’s live updates of the 2026 Republican National Convention

“If the Republicans win the House of Representatives and the United States Senate, both of them, because of our tremendous economic success… I will issue a dividend to every adult citizen in the United States of America for $5,000,” Trump said.

Donald Trump
7
President Trump takes the stage in Dallas to address the Republican midterm convention on Wednesday night.
Republican National Convention
The concept was “very much like a successful company will do a cash distribution to its shareholders,” he said.

“We’re going to give you that Trump dividend to $5,000 if we win, and we’re going to win.”

It’s unclear if the idea would pass muster with fiscal conservatives — as it would add more than $1.2 trillion to the already surging $40 trillion national debt.

In 2020, then-Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell (R-Ky.) blocked Trump’s request for $2,000 COVID-19 stimulus checks and made the sum $600 due to fear that printing so much money would devalue the currency.

President Joe Biden later approved the additional $1,400 — with critics saying it fueled an inflation crisis, which peaked at an annual rate of 9.1% in June 2022.

Other Trump-proposed direct payments haven’t been implemented, including plans last year for dividends funded with tariffs and cost savings from the DOGE drive to slash the federal bureaucracy.

Trump vowed a blizzard of new legislation for Republicans to pass in his final two years in office, including bills to end surprise medical billing, require hospital price transparency, slash fees that credit card companies charge on purchases, end state-level cashless bail policies and apply the death penalty for large-scale drug dealers.

He said he would continue to push for stalled national voter ID rules, continue to boost domestic energy production, make permanent his new tax cuts on tips, overtime and Social Security payments and pass legislation barring future presidents from returning to more lax Biden-era border policies.

GOP RNC Dallas
7
Preparations are made on stage at the Republican National Midterm Convention in Dallas, Texas, September 9, 2026.
REUTERS
“Your vote will decide whether our country stumbles at the starting gate of the next 250 years or surges forward and never ever looks back,” Trump told thousands of attendees inside the American Airlines Center, home to the NBA’s Dallas Mavericks.

He also toyed with renaming New Mexico “New America” and renaming the Strait of Hormuz after himself.

“Vote Republican and we will leave the world in our dust for generations to come,” Trump said.

GOP RNC midterms
7
Attendees react during the Republican National Midterm Convention in Dallas, Texas, U.S., September 9, 2026.
REUTERS
“We hand America’s future to the radical left Democrats, and our nation will spend the next decade just getting back on its feet,” he warned.

“I’m asking you to pretend that I’m on the ballot — just one more time, because if we lose, you’re going to lose your border, you’re going to lose your tax cuts, you’re going to lose your safety and security, you’re going to lose your wealth.”

Trump urged voters to consider that the Iran war is dragging on — harming Republicans with higher inflation and gas prices — because Tehran is “hoping that we lose so they can deal with dumb, weak Democrats and they can have their nuclear bomb.” 

He predicted the conflict would end shortly after the Nov. 3 vote, causing oil prices to plummet.

Split screen of John Fetterman in a black hoodie speaking in front of an industrial building, with a crowd at a political event on the left.
7
Fetterman appeared in a video praising fellow Pennsylvania senator Dave McCormick.
C-SPAN
‘Sick cloud over our country’
Trump said he plans to campaign at least once in all states with competitive House and Senate races to defend his agenda — and dispel the “sick cloud” of “communism,” especially in the 35 most hotly contested House races.

He interjected colorful attacks on various Democratic candidates, particularly those in Senate races, including James Talarico in Texas, Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan and Roy Cooper in North Carolina.

Cooper, he said, should see his support plunge, likening him to 1988 Democratic presidential candidate Michael Dukakis for allowing an “animal” repeat criminal offender to roam free before murdering Iryna Zarutska on public transit last year.

Playing comedian-in-chief, Trump noted that Talarico once promoted vegetarianism with a campaign called “beat meat,” humorously adding to laughter, “I don’t know what the hell he meant by that.”

El-Sayed, he said, was an “extremist” whose sister “celebrated the terrorist slaughter of babies on October 7th” and whose mother “worked for an organization that gave hundreds of thousands of dollars to people that follow Osama bin Laden.”

Trump spoke after Republicans cheered on five hours of warm-up acts, including up-and-coming congressional candidates and cabinet secretaries — competing with the opening night of the NFL season as the New England Patriots faced the Seattle Seahawks in a Super Bowl rematch.

UFC fighter Bo Nickal speaks at the Republican convention in Dallas on Thursday, Sept. 10, 2026.
7
UFC fighter Bo Nickal speaks at the Republican convention in Dallas on Thursday, Sept. 10, 2026.
AP Photo/Tony Gutierrez
“There is a crazy little sick cloud over our country,” Trump said, leaning into the event’s effort to link Democrats writ large with self-declared socialists who won a number of upsets in primary races this year.

“I really believe it’s not going anywhere, but we have to make sure because we will defeat communism in America and vote for American freedom.”

He spoke as Republicans court moderate voters and Hispanics, a voting bloc that polls show is drifting after surging support to Trump’s 2024 campaign, which pressed hard on an anti-socialist message and promises to tame inflation and illegal border crossings.

Fetterman, underwear pic shock attendees
The hastily planned “Trump-a-palooza” made good on hints of surprises.

Sen. John Fetterman (D-Pa.) appeared in a video denouncing “the extremes and socialism and that anti-American way of life” and praising Sen. Dave McCormick (R-Pa.), as speculation mounts that he will switch parties.

U.S. President Donald Trump speaks at the Republican National Midterm Convention.
7
U.S. President Donald Trump speaks at the Republican National Midterm Convention on Sept. 9, 2026, in Dallas, Texas.
REUTERS
Jumbo-screens also shockingly showed a half-naked selfie of anti-Israel commentator Hasan Piker — a close ally of Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed. The radical streamer’s tight blue underwear was blurred to obscure the still-visible anatomical contours underneath.

Justin Gaethje, the UFC fighter who won the headline match at the cage match on the White House lawn in June, appeared minutes ahead of Trump, saying the president “took the world by storm, similar to my chances on June 14” and praised the “leader who treats every day like I treated my fight that night.”

“Your next fight is the only one that matters,” he said. “We have to get out and vote… We risk getting knocked out.”

The 21,000-person arena swelled with guests ahead of Trump’s speech, though hundreds of nosebleed seats remained available.

Arizona Republican Congressional candidate Jay Feely speaking on stage at the Republican National Convention.
7
Arizona Republican Congressional candidate Jay Feely speaks on stage on the first day of the 2026 Republican National Convention at the American Airlines Center on September 9, 2026, in Dallas, Texas.
Getty Images
Trump announced the convention just over two months ago as a gamble to prevent an electoral bloodbath that would imperil his final two years in office. Republicans lost 41 House seats during the midterm election in his first term.

Democrats have vowed to block Trump’s agenda and investigate and possibly impeach him if they retake control in Congress.

The event had the feel of a traditional presidential-year convention — complete with state markers on the floor, zany costumes including many sequin jackets and enthusiastic dancing by party reps on camera to dated hits such as 1984’s “Footloose” by Kenny Loggins.

Republican leaders who spoke before Trump highlighted major elements of his agenda, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent receiving rousing applause before touting private-sector job gains and “Trump accounts” for newborns.

Medicare and Medicaid chief Dr. Mehmet Oz spoke about Trump’s efforts to lower prescription drug prices, saying “so many of you look like gazelles” due to expanded coverage for GLP-1 weight-loss drugs.

The event significantly served to raise the profiles of rising Republican stars.

The first speakers after an opening prayer were a pair of Mexican-American siblings running for House seats in Texas, Rep. Monica De La Cruz, whose district stretches south from San Antonio, and her brother, Carlos De La Cruz, who would rep a neighboring district.

Former Arizona Cardinals NFL player Jay Feely, who is running for the House in Arizona, and military veteran Mike Bouchard Jr., who is running in Michigan, were given prime slots.

House Majority Whip Tom Emmer (R-Minn.) told attendees the election was “between common sense and communism, between America-loving patriots and hate-America extremists.”

“The Communist Party, oh excuse me, the Democrats have no leader,” Emmer jabbed. “The only thing they can agree on is their disgusting hatred of America.”

LASER Index Management Charter

The main purpose of this document is to give you an understanding of how you can get the most value out of spending time with me via reading my posts, my research, and occasionally listening to my thoughts through, for instance, spaces or a podcast.

I wrote this so that you can receive the maximum value from my work and so that I can serve you to the best of my ability.

With that in mind, below, I will share something akin to a constitution for my work, which I deliver to you via this profile, Substack, and my online chats. I will also detail how I think about the panoply of ideas that I share with you so that you have ample context for my posts. It is the case today, and it will always be the case, that I share both stock research and philosophical/political thinking, as stocks are merely assets owned by a nation and its character. A business cannot thrive if the national character within which it operates is poorly structured, ailing, or deformed.

Before I share the enumerated points that represent the charter for LASER Index Management, I’d like to provide a brief introduction so that you can get to know me a little bit:

My name is Louis A. Stevens (hence, L.A. Stevens Equity Research, or LASER), and I live in the United States.

I have a political science degree, an MBA, and I served 10 years in the U.S. Army, eight of which were as an Engineer Officer, mostly as a reservist. 

I view having served as an Engineer Officer as one of my greatest life privileges. I love the sport of investing, and all the work I do today is mostly just fun for me. I do it all not because I have to, but because I genuinely love the sport of it. It is my favorite way to contribute to humanity.

Let’s now talk about LASER Index Management exclusively.

I run a model portfolio that I offer as a product to my Substack subscribers, and I call it the LASER Index, and I am the management of this Index, hence its name. This is a basket of 30-40 stocks, the number of which will grow over time. I believe in diversification that can outperform while mitigating risk.

The main goal of the Index, over the long term, is to outperform the QQQ, while offering my subscribers inspiration, frameworks, and templates as to how they too can replicate strong, consistent results in a relatively conservative manner. It is my strongly held view that the strategy that I will enumerate below is relatively conservative, though some may disagree, and I respect their disagreement; however, again, I strongly believe in this approach and its ability to manage risk over time, while producing strong returns.

With this as our platform, below, I will share a handful of bylaws that guide my work on this account, on Substack, and in my online chats. The main purpose of these bylaws is to help you get the most out of following this account. These points will help you better understand my thoughts and better employ my thoughts in such a way as to enhance your own investing operations.

1. The only “stock” I recommend is the entirety of the LASER Index comprehensively: its specific holdings and weightings. While I discuss a broad range of stocks publicly, sharing my stream of consciousness thinking at times, my only recommendation is and will always be the LASER Index in its entirety. Individual stocks and macroeconomic thinking that I share with you represent food-for-thought analysis, not standalone buy calls. To reiterate, my only recommendation is to buy the entirety of the LASER Index: all of its weightings and holdings exactly as they’re displayed in the Index. I share this so that you know exactly what I like at the exact prices and exact weightings at any given time. Zero confusion. No wondering. Direct, straightforward, reliable guidance, with a corresponding ledger of trades, holdings, and weightings. You can access the entirety of the LASER Index on my Substack, whose link is in the description of my profile.

2. I will routinely discuss various stocks, bonds, and macroeconomic perspectives with the intention of providing food-for-thought to my audience, encouraging thoughts for your own investment practices, and generally adding to the body of thought that is the collective consciousness of the market. Most of these thoughts will be with respect to stocks that I extract from the LASER Index itself, such as Amazon as a very basic example; for which I provide in-depth research reports on my Substack, but some may just be stocks that are popular, and to whose body of thought I’d like to add. The spirit of everything I do is serving you to the highest extent possible.

3. My ultimate goal is to deliver the LASER Index as a product to you and to the investment community broadly. That is my main focus. I take managing the index seriously, and I want to deliver a comprehensive, scalable investing strategy to my audience and subscribers. Secondarily, I hope to create the aforementioned content that is thought provoking, salutary, and broadly beneficial to your life. As I continue to reiterate, the spirit of all I do is service to you to the highest, most excellent extent possible.

4. Regarding the LASER Index’s strategy, I use a super straightforward, relatively conservative, exceedingly patient strategy to run the Index. The main pillar of my approach is identifying as many attractive investment setups (asymmetric risk/return setups) as possible. I work to, for instance, identify 30 as-close-to-identical risk/return setups, where I reason that risk is low and return potential is very high. I then allow the positions to grow over time in a survival-of-the-fittest fashion, creating concentration within the portfolio in the process. The businesses that perform well, executing and growing exceptionally, naturally grow into larger positions and begin to command authority over the rest of the portfolio and its returns, as is the natural course of business within a given industry in the economy. As the concentration forms, I mostly do nothing, allowing the best, winningest, and highest quality stocks to carry outperformance of the portfolio over time.

5. While I am a very patient investor, who strives to accumulate compelling businesses that I can hold forever, the reality is that it’s worth trading positions sometimes. Investment theses can change materially. The wheels can come off to an extent that requires either exiting the position or reducing the position’s size. Moreover, new, compelling companies emerge either by way of their own evolutions or via going public, and I may add these to the Index when I deem appropriate. So I do trade from time to time, and there is always a catalogue of all trades made since launch, which you can easily audit and trace with the help of AI.

6. The LASER Index is a generalist portfolio that reflects my view of the future, e.g., humans will continue to develop unique computing platforms such as virtual reality and will build a Space Empire over time. The Index holds restaurants, computing infrastructure, consumer credit, consumer discretionary, and a handful of international companies. I refer to it as a Supercomputer whose price action reflects the state of the global economy, and this is another benefit of the portfolio, i.e., its breadth in terms of industry and geography provides a lot of insight into the state of the global chessboard. It can be as much a macroeconomic signal as it can be a representation of the performance of the businesses it owns.

7. I am not a registered investment adviser, and none of what I say is personalized investment advice. I publish my research, alongside an always available model portfolio, to all subscribers at the same time. Nothing here is tailored to your circumstances, and I don't know your situation, goals, or risk tolerance. I cannot and will not give individual advice. I am not compensated by any company I write about, nor will I ever be. I try to remain skeptical of my companies’ operations so that I remain objective about their performance. I always disclose the LASER Index’s exact positioning via my research notes published to my Substack. All of my incentives are perfectly aligned with the LASER Index and its long term success, as, when it succeeds, you succeed; thereby, I succeed. Choose to follow along if you desire, and remember that stocks are risky. Business is risky. There are no guarantees for any business and its stock, no matter how bullish I, you, the CEO, or the market may be. Past performance does not guarantee future results. Remember to do your own due diligence.

8. Everything I do and share is a part of one overarching thread. Few, if any, ideas are randomly or haphazardly shared. They all weave together into one tapestry. If I share something philosophically or politically on my profile, you can be sure that it weaves into the tapestry of thought into which the LASER Index is woven also.

In summary, I am here to serve you. Everything I do is in service of you. My only stock recommendation is the LASER Index, whose weightings, trades, and holdings are disclosed on my Substack. I will discuss a wide range of topics on my profile, but they all tie together into one valuable tapestry of thought into which the LASER Index is woven also.

And, through this service to you, my goal is to enhance the quality of your life to the highest extent possible and to be an asset to you, so that you can be the best person to those in your life.

Thanks for reading, keep following along, and let me know if you have any questions, comments, or concerns.

The claim that Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has a cousin who is a “jihadi” is unsubstantiated. No court records, official statements, or reporting from established news organisations identify any such relative or document any terrorism-related conviction or designation involving a member of her family.
The video offered as proof recounts a 2015 recording of former British Army captain Afzal Amin, then a Conservative parliamentary candidate. Amin was filmed discussing a planned EDL protest that he hoped to take credit for resolving. Contemporary coverage treated the episode as a political sting, not a terrorism case; Amin was never charged with terrorism offences. The later assertion of a first-cousin relationship with Mahmood and the inference that this connection explains later prison decisions remain unverified by independent sources.
Unproven allegations linking a serving minister’s family to jihadism are serious. In the absence of evidence they amount to rumour, not fact.

Crypto peak!?

The crypto market has broken out of its consolidation

Market Overview

The cryptocurrency market has risen by almost 8% over the past 24 hours to $2.37T, reaching its highest level since early June. The initial momentum came on the back of news that the US Treasury was supporting the debt market. This relatively small but timely move signalled that the government is monitoring the situation in the debt markets, spurring demand for risk assets. The rally was then fuelled by a wave of short-covering, following weeks of extremely narrow trading.

Bitcoin reached $70K, posting a 9% rally over 8 hours during the US trading session. As the new day began, the leading cryptocurrency retreated slightly to $69.6K. On Monday, BTC consolidated above the 50-day moving average, and by Wednesday, it had already tested the 200-day MA. As expected, the market’s long-compressed spring snapped back, catching those who had been range-trading and those who had been building short positions on the rise off guard. If Bitcoin does not quickly lose its recent gains, it will be a significant sign that a bull market has begun, much like in October 2023 or March 2020.

Ethereum recorded an even more impressive breakout, showing an 18% gain over 24 hours at its peak. Having risen to $2.25K, the second-largest cryptocurrency is trading near its April–May highs, having broken above its 200-day moving average and away from a long-term support line that has risen from around $1.75K to $1.9K over the past 8 months. The next significant level where the coin may face resistance to further gains appears to be the $2.5K–$2.8K range. (FxPro)

Alphabet’s stake in Anthropic expands

The value of Alphabet’s stake in the artificial intelligence start-up Anthropic has soared to around $US124 billion ($178 billion), making it one of the most lucrative bets in the company’s history.The Google parent disclosed in a filing on Thursday (Friday AEST) that the value of its investments in unidentified private companies totalled roughly $US124.3 billion as of June 30. The filing noted that this value is “primarily” driven by one investment, which is a reference to Alphabet’s stake in Anthropic, according to a person familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified because the information is not public. The company said it recorded about $US77 billion in unrealised gains from its private investments in the second quarter, without providing further details in the filing. Google has emerged as one of Anthropic’s biggest backers over the past several years. The technology giant first invested $US3 billion in the start-up starting in 2023. Earlier this year, it agreed to invest as much as $US40 billion more, consisting of $US10 billion upfront and a potential $US30 billion in additional funding tied to operational and financial milestones through 2030.Alphabet’s filing on Thursday showed the remaining commitment has fallen to $US20 billion as of June 30 from $US30 billion at the end of the first quarter, suggesting that Google invested another $US10 billion in the start-up last quarter. News Flashback

Mining/Energy/Resources/Biz

Rio Tinto dodges merger bullet

Rio Tinto has dodged two 'bullets' due to Glencore's rejection of a merger proposal: a possible BHP takeover bid and a dangerous acquisition. BHP looked closely at whether to bid for Rio Tinto if the latter announced a merger with Glencore. The two companies would make excellent merger partners; amongst others things, their staff and senior people have similar cultures, they are co-operating on future Australian iron ore projects and they are copper joint venture partners in Chile and the US. Meanwhile, there are significance cultural differences between Rio Tinto and Glencore; there is little doubt that Rio Tinto's CEO Simon Trott would have had doubts about a merger once he understood these cultural differences. (RMS)

News/Snapshot

Australian Mining

Global Commodity Rankings

Australia holds some of the world's largest reserves and is a leading producer of several key minerals.

#1 Producer: Iron Ore, Bauxite, Lithium, Rutile, and Zircon.

#1 Reserves: Iron Ore, Gold, Lead, Nickel, Rutile, Uranium, and Zinc.

#2 Producer: Gold, Alumina, and Manganese.

Key Mining Hubs & Major Projects

Western Australia: The nation's "engine room," producing 98% of Australia's iron ore and 60% of its gold. Major sites include the Pilbara (iron ore) and the Super Pit in Kalgoorlie (gold).

Queensland: A global leader in metallurgical coal (Bowen Basin) and silver/lead production (Cannington mine).

South Australia: Home to Olympic Dam, which contains the world's largest single uranium deposit and significant copper and gold reserves.

Major Players

The sector is dominated by several multinational giants and significant domestic players:

BHP: Often ranked as Australia's most valuable company; major interests in iron ore, copper, and coal.

Rio Tinto: A world leader in iron ore (Pilbara) and aluminum.

Fortescue (FMG): Primarily focused on iron ore and rapidly expanding into green energy.

Hancock Prospecting: Australia's largest private mining company, led by Gina Rinehart, the nation's wealthiest person.

text:
As above, so below.

Today Europe committed 131 billion euros to defence, security and space in next year's budget. Five times the current level, and another five billion to scale up strategic technologies. 

French President @EmmanuelMacron called for European demand to be pooled across operators, satellite builders and launcher companies. 

The Director General of @esa, @AschbacherJosef set out an increased capacity with European rockets, crew vehicles and launch systems as a platform Europe can offer the world.

It is a serious programme and it deserves to succeed. Here is the part nobody said out loud today.

In the 1970s and 1980s, geologists drilled a rare earth deposit at Storkwitz in Saxony, over and over. They mapped it, and documented it, and then walked away, because the cost of reaching the rock was higher than the price of importing it.

Forty years later, the same continent is voting 131 billion euros for programmes that cannot be built without that rock.

Niobium in the nozzle extension, roughly 90% of world production in Brazil. 

Germanium under every solar array, around 60% of global production is located in China and under export licence since 2023. 

Tantalum in the flight electronics, with Congo and Rwanda at about 63% of world mine production. 

Rare earths in every magnet, and Europe imports 100%.

Europe is not short of deposits. It is short of a reason to reach them, and that reason has always been cost.
 
We at @Hades are changing that.

We hold the exploration licence over Storkwitz today, and the technology - our proprietary laser drill - to make deposits like it economic.

text:
September 10, 2025.
Wednesday morning in Hawaii.

I was in the middle of helping a client purchase a multimillion-dollar home—one of the most luxurious homes in the area.

We had gone back and forth several times: offer, counteroffer, and another counteroffer.

The night before, we had submitted our final counteroffer. Both sides were sincere, and the deal looked promising. The seller’s deadline to respond was noon.

I was waiting.

That was when the devastating news came: Charlie Kirk had been killed.

It hit me like a blow to the chest. I couldn’t believe it. I didn’t want to believe it.

I was in the kitchen making coffee and breakfast. I held onto the counter and cried quietly.

I couldn’t stop.

But the phone still had to be answered. Texts still had to be returned. Terms still had to be confirmed. My client was still waiting.

Grief does not pause because you have a multimillion-dollar deal on the table.

Work does not wait because your heart is breaking.

I kept going—negotiating, communicating, and following up. During the calls, I tried to keep my voice steady while swallowing my tears.

Finally, we got the deal done.

My client had just secured their dream home—a moment that should have been filled with celebration.

But I couldn’t celebrate.

I was grief-stricken. I felt that I had lost someone I deeply respected and admired—and that the world had lost a hero and an extraordinary leader.

A year later, I want to write about the Charlie Kirk I saw—and why losing him hurt this much.

Next: For Charlie.

Happy Thursday! It’s time for another morning forecast discussion! Highs today will climb into the mid to upper 90s for most of us under partly cloudy skies. There will be an opportunity for a few very isolated showers or thunderstorms during peak daytime heating this afternoon, but there’s a pretty good chance most, if not all, of us stay dry. Better rain chances will remain off to our north.

Things begin changing heading into Friday and Saturday as a stationary front slowly approaches Southern Middle Tennessee from the north and west. That will increase our rain chances pretty substantially, and right now, Saturday looks about as close to a washout as we’ve had in quite a while, especially during the afternoon.

Now, this “stationary front” isn’t truly stationary. It’s just moving realllyyyy slow. Kind of like the folks taking their 50 MPH Sunday stroll in the left lane on Highway 231 where the speed limit is 65. I said what I said!

Anyways... Because this front will be moving so slowly, it will keep elevated rain chances around for several days. Scattered showers and thunderstorms will become more common Friday and Saturday, with additional rain chances likely continuing into next week. But our stationary front will dissipate, so we'll be left with isolated activity compared to scattered.

The key word(s) here are ISOLATED and SCATTERED. Showers and storms will generally favor the afternoon and evening hours. This means rainfall will not be evenly distributed. Y'all know how this works. So, don’t come at me if it rains at your house... and don’t come at me if it doesn’t rain at your house either!

Rainfall totals through the weekend will generally range from around a quarter-inch to one inch, although locally higher amounts will certainly be possible where thunderstorms repeatedly develop or move over the same areas.

Once this front finally clears, high pressure looks to build right back into the region. And high pressure this time of year means one thing... EVEN MORE “SWAMP BUTT” WEATHER.

Temperatures will remain quite warm through the weekend, with heat index values approaching 100° during the afternoon. Then, as high pressure strengthens early next week, the heat could really crank back up. By Tuesday and Wednesday, heat index values could approach or exceed 105° in parts of Southern Middle Tennessee.

So basically, we’re going from hot... to stormy and humid... and then right back to REALLY hot and humid. WOOHOO (NOT)!

text:
Yousri Belgaroui vs. Djorden Santos

Yousri Belgaroui 
At 34 years old (born June 2, 1992), the 6'6" orthodox fighter (79" reach) from Amsterdam, Netherlands (trains at Teixeira MMA & Fitness in Bethel, Connecticut under Glover Teixeira, alongside Alex Pereira) enters with a pro MMA record of 10-3. He has 8 KO/TKOs and 2 decisions. UFC record sits at 2-0.

Background and path: Dutch-Tunisian. University of Amsterdam graduate in organizational and public governance who worked security in Amsterdam and has done Dutch TV punditry. Turned pro in kickboxing in 2014 under Mike Passenier at Mike’s Gym. Compiled a 27-7 kickboxing record with 13 KOs, won a European title at 86kg, and challenged three times for the Glory middleweight title (all stoppage losses: cut TKO to Pereira at Glory 49, KO to Pereira at Glory 55, doctor stoppage to Donovan Wisse at Glory 78). Beat Pereira by decision in the Glory 40 contender tournament final, and lost twice to Israel Adesanya. Left kickboxing after 2021 and started MMA in January 2021 on UAE Warriors cards. Early MMA featured measuring, potshotting, and finishing power mixed with decision losses to Ahmed Sami (split) and Mohamad Osseili (unanimous) when opponents mixed wrestling and clinch work. Won the Levels Fight League light heavyweight title over Sami in a five-round rematch. First Contender Series appearance was a unanimous-decision loss to Marco Tulio in August 2023. Second Contender Series appearance was a third-round TKO of Taiga Iwasaki in September 2024 (point deducted for eye pokes) that did not immediately produce a contract. UFC debut TKO of Azamat Bekoev (October 2025, Vancouver) and TKO of previously undefeated Mansur Abdul-Malik (March 2026, Seattle). Has never been finished in MMA. Relocated his family to Connecticut in 2022 specifically to close grappling gaps after the Abu Dhabi losses.

Strengths: Elite range striking for the division. Jab, calf/outside leg kicks, body kicks, teeps, question-mark kicks, spinning attacks, flying knees, and especially stepping knees in the pocket or as a takedown deterrent. High accuracy (64% significant-strike accuracy) and a large output-to-absorption gap (6.10 SLpM, 2.17 SApM, 63% strike defense). Proven late-fight finishing: both UFC wins came in round 3 after he had already won the first two frames on damage and volume (102-24 striking vs. Bekoev, and 94-16 and two knockdowns vs. Abdul-Malik). Decent reactive takedown defense and get-ups when he frames, knees the shooter, or walls up (stuffed 4 of 8 vs. Bekoev and 3 of 8 vs. Abdul-Malik). Cardio to five rounds shown vs. Sami. Zero career finishes against him.

Weaknesses: Still a converted kickboxer more than a complete MMA fighter. Can measure and potshot for long stretches instead of chaining pressure. Tall-man defensive lapses and occasional over-commitment to kicks leave him hittable (tagged and dropped by Sami’s overhand in their first fight, outworked and taken down by Tulio across three rounds). Offensive wrestling is almost nonexistent (0.29 TD avg, one landed takedown in UFC). When a wrestler actually chains shots and stays on a single or body lock, he has grabbed the cage, given up control time, and lost rounds (Diani, Osseili, Tulio, portions of Bekoev and Abdul-Malik). Three losses are all decisions to opponents who either mixed takedowns or simply out-landed him in a firefight.

Djorden Santos 
At 29 years old (born August 1, 1997), the 6'0" orthodox fighter (75.5" reach) from Belo Horizonte/Trindade, Minas Gerais, Brazil (trains at American Top Team in Coconut Creek, Florida) enters with a pro record of 11-3. He has 3 KO/TKOs, 4 submissions, and 4 decisions. UFC record sits at 1-2.

Background and path: Left home at 14 to train full-time after a stretch as an overweight teenager in a Goiás organized supporters’ group. Mother sent about $60 a week. Worked as a grill cook, security, tent assembler, and iFood delivery driver. Started training around 2013 to channel aggression. Boxed first (district team, represented Brazil in Europe). Pro MMA debut March 2015. First five fights produced four submissions (RNC, two arm-triangles, guillotine). Lost a unanimous decision to Cristian Torres at Titan FC 52 in January 2019, then sat out two and a half years, ballooned, and came back at heavyweight with two finishes in two weeks in 2021 (Oliveira, Chicao). Won the Thunder Fight title over Filipe Moitinho in a five-round decision in November 2022 after a late opponent change. Earned a UFC contract with a unanimous decision over Will Currie on Contender Series 2024 Week 4. UFC debut unanimous-decision loss to Ozzy Diaz at UFC 313 (March 2025). Dropped to welterweight and won a unanimous decision over Danny Barlow in Vancouver (October 2025). Back at middleweight, submitted by Baisangur Susurkaev via rear-naked choke at 4:12 of round 3 at UFC 328 (May 2026). Stepping in on short notice here after Kelvin Gastelum withdrew. Brown belt in BJJ. Last finish was August 2021. Has never been knocked out.

Strengths: Chin and willingness to stand in the pocket. Went the distance in wars with Diaz (131-135 significant strikes) and Barlow (99-93) and bloodied Susurkaev in round 2 before the late choke. High output (6.64 SLpM in UFC). Boxing-based 1-2s, hooks, overhands, body work, and calf kicks. Solid takedown defense in the Octagon (85% TDD, stuffed most of what Diaz, Barlow, and Susurkaev offered until the final sequence). Early-career submission finishing (four of first five wins). Five-round gas tank shown vs. Moitinho. Recovers and keeps throwing after being hurt.

Weaknesses: Striking defense is porous (49% significant-strike defense). Eats nearly as much as he lands (6.35 SApM). Linear entries and a habit of planting in the pocket rather than angling off. Offensive wrestling has almost disappeared at this level: 1 takedown landed on 7 attempts across three UFC fights, 0.51 TD avg, 14-28% accuracy. Last five wins are decisions. Grappling offense that produced early-career submissions has not shown up recently. Susurkaev eventually put him on the fence, slammed a single, took the back, and choked him unconscious. Short-notice camp against a much taller southpaw-range problem (he is orthodox) after a May finish loss. Accuracy sits at 43%.

Stylistic Breakdown & Key Matchup Factors

Size & physicality: This is the clearest physical mismatch on the prelims. Belgaroui is 6'6" with a 79" reach, while Santos is 6'0" with a 75.5" reach. That is six inches of height and three-and-a-half inches of reach, plus a much longer leg. Belgaroui has used that frame to kick calves, stab jabs, and knee entries against every recent opponent. Santos has not faced this kind of length in the UFC. Clinch strength is closer, as Santos can lean, dirty-box, and wall-walk very well, but he has to get there first.

Striking: Belgaroui is the clearer technician and the far more efficient striker. His tape is built on measuring, calf kicks that accumulate, jabs that flatten noses, body kicks, and knees that end nights. Accuracy and defense numbers back it: 64% landed, 63% defended. Santos throws a lot and will stand there with anyone, but he absorbs clean shots doing it and his head-hunting (83% of UFC significant strikes to the head) plays into a taller man who counters with knees and check hooks. Santos’ best standing looks are the overhand and the 1-2 when opponents stay in the pocket. Belgaroui’s best looks are the exact shots that have finished Pretorius, Kvelidze, Iwasaki, Bekoev, and Abdul-Malik: the stepping knee and the right hand after the calf kick. Edge clearly to Belgaroui on the feet if the fight stays at range.

Grappling/Wrestling: This is the only realistic path for Santos, and the recent tape does not show him taking it. Early in his career he finished four of five with submissions. In the UFC he has landed one takedown in three fights. Susurkaev is the one who finally put him on the mat and ended him. Belgaroui is not a wrestler, but he has stuffed the majority of shots, kneed shooters in the face, and stood up quickly when taken down. The holes are real: Tulio wizzered him, stayed on top, and won 30-27, Osseili and Diani found control time. Those holes matter if Santos actually chains singles, body locks, and mat returns the way he did against Moitinho years ago. They matter less if Santos does what he has done since arriving in the UFC: stand and trade. Slight edge to Santos in finishing threat if he gets on the back or in mount. Edge to Belgaroui in keeping the fight standing based on recent habits of both men.

Pace & cardio: Both have gone long. Belgaroui looked fresh through five rounds against Sami and through two-plus against Bekoev and Abdul-Malik before the finishes. Santos went five with Moitinho and three hard ones with Diaz, Barlow, and Susurkaev. Santos’ output holds... his defense does not. If this becomes a high-pace striking match, Belgaroui’s accuracy and damage rate should create the kind of accumulating calf/body/knee damage that folded Abdul-Malik’s lead leg and then his posture. Santos’ chin and refusal to go away are the variables that keep rounds from ending early.

Intangibles

Same Vancouver card: Both fought on UFC Fight Night 262 in October 2025. Belgaroui finished Bekoev early in round 3 after controlling the first two.

Finishes: Belgaroui’s last three wins are all TKOs in round 3 or the last seconds of round 1 (Kvelidze). Santos has not finished anyone recently.

Prepared versus replacement: Belgaroui was building toward Kelvin Gastelum. Santos took this on short notice after Gastelum withdrew. That does not automatically decide a fight, but it does mean Santos is stepping up in weight class context and length of opponent with less time to solve a 6'6" kickboxer who lives behind a jab and a calf kick.

Disciplinary habits: Belgaroui has eye-poke and cage-grab moments on tape (Iwasaki point deduction; blatant fence grab vs. Diani). Is it relative here? Maybe, maybe not... but worth mentioning.

Wise Prediction

Belgaroui should keep this at kicking range, chop the lead leg, stab the jab, and treat any level change as a knee opportunity. Santos will try to walk him down, trade 1-2s, and look for the overhand when Belgaroui kicks. His path to winning is forcing a pocket brawl or finally using the wrestling he showed on the regional scene: chain a single, stay attached, take the back.

Belgaroui is not a great mixed martial artist. Tulio exposed the wrestling holes, Sami dropped him with an overhand, and he still measures too much. Those facts matter less against an opponent whose UFC identity is stand-and-bang with 49% strike defense and one landed takedown in three fights. Santos’ chin and motor make a firefight live. They do not make him the better striker, and they do not magically restore a grappling attack he has not featured since before his UFC run.

My pick: Yousri Belgaroui by KO/TKO in R2 or R3 (or decision if Santos turns it into a clinch grind).

Why? The length, calf-kick cycle, jab, and knees are the cleanest tools in the matchup, and they are the tools Belgaroui has actually used to finish the last several men who tried to walk him down. Santos can take a shot and keep coming like a zombie as one announcer put it, but walking into a 79-inch reach with 49% defense is how those late-round knees find the jaw. Santos only flips this if he wrestles like 2016-2022 Santos instead of 2025-2026 Santos. Nothing in the last four fights says that is the plan.

Best bet angle: Primary lean is Belgaroui on the moneyline. His range, accuracy, damage rate, and finishing pattern against advancing opponents are the most repeatable edges here. Belgaroui by KO/TKO (especially R2/R3) is the method that matches both his recent tape and Santos’ habit of staying in the pocket after the calf kicks pile up while having a granite chin. Over 2.5 rounds is live because Santos’ chin and motor have carried him into third rounds against better athletes than the regional names Belgaroui used to flatten early. Under 2.5 is the length if the first calf-kick or knee sequence lands clean. Santos by decision is the underdog path that requires him to wrestle or win ugly pocket rounds, and Santos by submission is the highest-variance longshot and needs a version of his grappling that has not appeared anywhere in years.

Market Overview

The cryptocurrency market has risen by almost 8% over the past 24 hours to $2.37T, reaching its highest level since early June. The initial momentum came on the back of news that the US Treasury was supporting the debt market. This relatively small but timely move signalled that the government is monitoring the situation in the debt markets, spurring demand for risk assets. The rally was then fuelled by a wave of short-covering, following weeks of extremely narrow trading.

Bitcoin reached $70K, posting a 9% rally over 8 hours during the US trading session. As the new day began, the leading cryptocurrency retreated slightly to $69.6K. On Monday, BTC consolidated above the 50-day moving average, and by Wednesday, it had already tested the 200-day MA. As expected, the market’s long-compressed spring snapped back, catching those who had been range-trading and those who had been building short positions on the rise off guard. If Bitcoin does not quickly lose its recent gains, it will be a significant sign that a bull market has begun, much like in October 2023 or March 2020.

Ethereum recorded an even more impressive breakout, showing an 18% gain over 24 hours at its peak. Having risen to $2.25K, the second-largest cryptocurrency is trading near its April–May highs, having broken above its 200-day moving average and away from a long-term support line that has risen from around $1.75K to $1.9K over the past 8 months. The next significant level where the coin may face resistance to further gains appears to be the $2.5K–$2.8K range. (FxPro)

Alphabet’s stake in Anthropic expands

The value of Alphabet’s stake in the artificial intelligence start-up Anthropic has soared to around $US124 billion ($178 billion), making it one of the most lucrative bets in the company’s history.The Google parent disclosed in a filing on Thursday (Friday AEST) that the value of its investments in unidentified private companies totalled roughly $US124.3 billion as of June 30. The filing noted that this value is “primarily” driven by one investment, which is a reference to Alphabet’s stake in Anthropic, according to a person familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified because the information is not public. The company said it recorded about $US77 billion in unrealised gains from its private investments in the second quarter, without providing further details in the filing. Google has emerged as one of Anthropic’s biggest backers over the past several years. The technology giant first invested $US3 billion in the start-up starting in 2023. Earlier this year, it agreed to invest as much as $US40 billion more, consisting of $US10 billion upfront and a potential $US30 billion in additional funding tied to operational and financial milestones through 2030.Alphabet’s filing on Thursday showed the remaining commitment has fallen to $US20 billion as of June 30 from $US30 billion at the end of the first quarter, suggesting that Google invested another $US10 billion in the start-up last quarter. Rio Tinto dodges merger bullet

Rio Tinto has dodged two 'bullets' due to Glencore's rejection of a merger proposal: a possible BHP takeover bid and a dangerous acquisition. BHP looked closely at whether to bid for Rio Tinto if the latter announced a merger with Glencore. The two companies would make excellent merger partners; amongst others things, their staff and senior people have similar cultures, they are co-operating on future Australian iron ore projects and they are copper joint venture partners in Chile and the US. Meanwhile, there are significance cultural differences between Rio Tinto and Glencore; there is little doubt that Rio Tinto's CEO Simon Trott would have had doubts about a merger once he understood these cultural differences. News/Snapshot

Australian Mining

Global Commodity Rankings

Australia holds some of the world's largest reserves and is a leading producer of several key minerals.

#1 Producer: Iron Ore, Bauxite, Lithium, Rutile, and Zircon.

#1 Reserves: Iron Ore, Gold, Lead, Nickel, Rutile, Uranium, and Zinc.

#2 Producer: Gold, Alumina, and Manganese.

Key Mining Hubs & Major Projects

Western Australia: The nation's "engine room," producing 98% of Australia's iron ore and 60% of its gold. Major sites include the Pilbara (iron ore) and the Super Pit in Kalgoorlie (gold).

Queensland: A global leader in metallurgical coal (Bowen Basin) and silver/lead production (Cannington mine).

South Australia: Home to Olympic Dam, which contains the world's largest single uranium deposit and significant copper and gold reserves.

Major Players

The sector is dominated by several multinational giants and significant domestic players:

BHP: Often ranked as Australia's most valuable company; major interests in iron ore, copper, and coal.

Rio Tinto: A world leader in iron ore (Pilbara) and aluminum.

Fortescue (FMG): Primarily focused on iron ore and rapidly expanding into green energy.

Hancock Prospecting: Australia's largest private mining company, led by Gina Rinehart, the nation's wealthiest person.

South32: Spun out of BHP; manages a diversified portfolio including manganese, silver, and nickel.

2026 Trends & Developments

Critical Minerals Push: The government has introduced a $23 billion package to support domestic processing and manufacturing of critical minerals to reduce global reliance on single-country supply chains.

Uranium Rally: Prices exceeding US$100/lb have sparked renewed interest in Australian prospects like the Kalkaroo project.

M&A Activity: Major merger talks continue between giants like Rio Tinto and Glencore as they seek to consolidate copper exposure for the EV market.

Workforce Challenges: The Minerals Council of Australia is currently calling for migration reforms to address a significant "skills crunch" in the sector.

Australian Mining

Global Commodity Rankings

Australia holds some of the world's largest reserves and is a leading producer of several key minerals.

#1 Producer: Iron Ore, Bauxite, Lithium, Rutile, and Zircon.

#1 Reserves: Iron Ore, Gold, Lead, Nickel, Rutile, Uranium, and Zinc.

#2 Producer: Gold, Alumina, and Manganese.

Key Mining Hubs & Major Projects

Western Australia: The nation's "engine room," producing 98% of Australia's iron ore and 60% of its gold. Major sites include the Pilbara (iron ore) and the Super Pit in Kalgoorlie (gold).

Queensland: A global leader in metallurgical coal (Bowen Basin) and silver/lead production (Cannington mine).

South Australia: Home to Olympic Dam, which contains the world's largest single uranium deposit and significant copper and gold reserves.

Major Players

The sector is dominated by several multinational giants and significant domestic players:

BHP: Often ranked as Australia's most valuable company; major interests in iron ore, copper, and coal.

Rio Tinto: A world leader in iron ore (Pilbara) and aluminum.

Fortescue (FMG): Primarily focused on iron ore and rapidly expanding into green energy.

Hancock Prospecting: Australia's largest private mining company, led by Gina Rinehart, the nation's wealthiest person.

South32: Spun out of BHP; manages a diversified portfolio including manganese, silver, and nickel.

2026 Trends & Developments

Jimmy Kimmel told Wednesday night’s “Live” audience that his Thursday interview with James Talarico, the Democratic Senate nominee from Texas, would not air on television, but would instead be posted on YouTube.
The “unusual circumstances” of the interview, Kimmel said, were prompted by the Federal Communications Commission’s actions under President Trump, which Kimmel said had “threatened our show, threatened our network, ABC, our affiliates, our local stations, based on simple, traditional, editorial decisions — guest bookings it would seem they don’t like.”

Under guidance released in January,the F.C.C. warned that entertainment-oriented talk shows carried on local TV stations were required to offer equal airtime to candidates running for the same office.

“You know, for a lot of years, for the whole 20-plus years of our show, in fact, I’ve been interviewing Americans who are running for office with no problem at all, just like Letterman did, Leno did, Arsenio, etc. etc.,” Jimmy Kimmel said.

“I interviewed Donald Trump when he was running for president in 2015, and at that time, when he was the one sitting next to me, he seemed to have no problem with the idea of talk show hosts interviewing candidates. text:
Mythology Drop: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre

The Texas Chain Saw Massacre is one of the purest and most influential pieces of modern American folk-horror mythology. Released in 1974 and directed by Tobe Hooper, it presents itself with the cold authority of a true crime document while constructing a nightmare that feels older than the film itself.

The Core Legend
In the rural backroads of Texas, a group of young people encounter a isolated family of slaughterhouse workers who have turned their trade inward. The most infamous member is the figure known as Leatherface — a hulking, nearly speechless man who wears masks stitched from human skin and wields a roaring chainsaw. Around him exists an entire household of cannibals and scavengers who have made a grotesque domestic life from the remains of their victims.

The story unfolds less like a conventional narrative and more like a descent into a private underworld: a house decorated with bones and furniture made of human remains, a family dinner that is both absurd and horrific, and the relentless pursuit of the final girl through sun-bleached fields and darkened rooms. The chainsaw itself becomes a mythic tool — industrial, mechanical, and intimate at once.

Origins and Influences
Though the film opens with the claim that it is based on true events, the story is largely fictional. Its deepest root is the real-life crimes of Ed Gein, the Wisconsin grave robber and murderer whose house of human trophies inspired both Psycho and The Texas Chain Saw Massacre. Hooper and writer Kim Henkel transformed that source material into something distinctly Texan and modern: a vision of rural America as a place where the old order of family, work, and meat has collapsed into something feral.

The film was made on a tiny budget in the brutal Texas heat. That physical hardship bled into the finished work, giving it a raw, almost documentary texture that helped the myth take hold. Audiences left theaters believing they had witnessed something closer to reportage than fiction.

Themes of the Myth
The story operates on several levels at once. It is a nightmare of the American family turned inside out — a household that still gathers for dinner even as it consumes outsiders. It is also a meditation on the meat industry and the violence hidden inside ordinary labor. The slaughterhouse background of the family is never far from the surface; the chainsaw is simply the tool that has moved from animal carcasses to human ones.

There is a strong current of Vietnam-era dread in the film: the sense that something has gone wrong in the heart of the country, that the young are being fed into a machine that no longer distinguishes between enemy and neighbor. The rural landscape itself becomes hostile — empty roads, abandoned houses, and the relentless Texas sun that offers no safety.

Legacy
Leatherface joined the pantheon of modern horror icons alongside figures like Michael Myers and Jason Voorhees, yet he remains distinct. He is less a supernatural force than a product of place and family pathology. The original film spawned sequels, remakes, and a sprawling expanded universe, but the 1974 original retains a unique power. It feels less like entertainment than a transmission from a darker America that still exists just off the main road.

In the landscape of contemporary mythology, The Texas Chain Saw Massacre endures as a cautionary tale about isolation, the collapse of community, and the places where the ordinary becomes monstrous. The chainsaw still echoes.

text:
Dr @ShashiTharoor articulates India should treat a deeper, structured partnership with Europe as a core tool of strategic autonomy — not as a replacement for the US, but as a hedge against an unpredictable Washington and a coercive China.
Tharoor’s argument is that mid-2020s geopolitics has made the old US-centric bet fragile. Tariffs, energy-policy pressure, and sudden swings in American policy have injected volatility into a relationship that once felt structurally predictable. Multi-alignment is therefore no longer optional: Quad, Gulf, Singapore, and others matter, but the EU is the missing large, high-capacity partner.
The January 2025 India–EU FTA (“mother of all deals”) is the economic pillar — 2 billion consumers, roughly a quarter of world GDP, tariffs cut or eliminated on ~96% of goods, plus rules on services, digital trade, and tech. For India it is a buffer against protectionism and a premium market; for Europe it is the flagship of “China Plus One” diversification.
The security pillar is the new Security and Defence Partnership: maritime and cyber cooperation, counter-terrorism, AI, access to Europe’s €150 billion defence initiative, joint production, and technology transfer. Europe cannot match US military or financial hegemony, but it offers what the US currently does not: institutional stability, technological depth, and policy predictability. Shared concern over Chinese coercion in sea lanes and connectivity projects makes the fit practical, not merely rhetorical.
Thus true autonomy is not isolation or passive non-alignment. It is active, overlapping, high-value partnerships. Binding India’s economic future to the FTA and its security architecture to Europe creates a double hedge — against Chinese assertiveness in the neighbourhood and against erratic American engagement. Two large democracies, in this reading, can become an anchor of a rules-based order when both great-power alternatives look less reliable.

Dear members of the American press!

Steve Jobs once said, "If you can convince the press of your technology, and the press convinces us, we'll pay attention."

That's why I'm reaching out to you.

For years, the development of personal devices has been driven by advances in smartphones, tablets, and virtual reality technologies. However, all of these solutions still require people to adapt to the device. I've developed a concept based on the opposite principle: the device should adapt to the user and interact with them as naturally as possible.

I believe this technology has the potential to be the next major step in the development of consumer electronics. It offers a fundamentally new way to interact with the digital environment and has the potential to replace many existing devices that accompany people in their daily lives today.

If my assessment is correct, this isn't just another gadget, but a platform capable of transforming the market in the same way that the personal computer, iPod, and iPhone once did. Such opportunities arise extremely rarely, and that's why they deserve independent attention and objective assessment.

I believe Apple has the experience, engineering culture, and vision necessary to turn this idea into a world-class product. Moreover, the successful implementation of such technology could strengthen the leadership of the American tech industry at a time when global competition is becoming increasingly fierce.

I'm not asking you to take my word for it. I'm asking only one thing: help draw Apple's attention to this development and give it the opportunity to be considered by those capable of objectively assessing its potential.

If the technology truly represents the value I see in it, ignoring it could be a missed opportunity. If not, that will become clear after a professional evaluation. But in either case, the idea deserves to be heard.

Thank you for your attention.

Sincerely,

Alexander.

text:
Su-57 is a flop show.

Rafale is a flop show.

Shift the focus to AMCA, Tejas and Kaveri or all three will be dead soon. If too pressing take Rafales or Su-57 on Lease. Why buying and keeping on head for 30 years? Even if buying Su-57 & Rafales first allot permanently non transferable fund for own projects like AMCA, Tejas & Kaveri so that these projects doesnt stall or fail due to foreign fighter purchase or lease.

​Instead of taking the bait talk to the GCAP team and offer what they are actually looking for.

​Masala news is everywhere. Is the Su-57E stealing the spotlight while Rafales leak tech? Social media algorithms are working overtime to push a narrative.

​China is training with Rafales in Egypt but notice how they aren't training with Su-57s there? They are already. The social media campaign for Su-57 is in full swing and algorithms are promoting it aggressively.

​Before falling for the Su-57 hype answer these critical questions:

​Impact on Domestic R&D: Will buying the Su-57 stall our indigenous AMCA, Tejas and Kaveri projects?

​Leasing Alternative: If we need a stopgap why can’t we take the Su-57 on lease instead of buying?

​Generational Gap: Isn't the Su-57 effectively a 4.5 generation fighter? How will it counter Chinese 5th and 6th gen fighters?

​Engine Lifespan: Is the Su-57 engine life half that of the F-35 and Western fighters effectively doubling the long term operational cost?

​Intel Risks: How much Su-57 technology does China already know given their decades long use of Russian platforms? Pakistani pilots trained on Rafales in Qatar and Chinese pilots trained in Egypt. What about the Su-57?

​Stealth vs. Maneuverability: Su-57 maneuverability is impressive but what about its radar cross section (RCS) and stealth? Stealth determines survival in modern warfare maneuverability comes second.

​The ToT Illusion: Everyone talks about Transfer of Technology (ToT) but ToT in what exactly? What is the percentage of ToT in engine manufacturing and single crystal blade metallurgy? Getting ToT for airframes or tires means nothing without core engine technology.

​Chinese Supply Chain Dependence: How many Su-57 parts originate in China? Will India become dependent on Chinese supply chains if local manufacturing starts? In a conflict China could cut off spares or share counter tech with Pakistan.

​Strategic Trap: If we invest heavily in Su-57 infrastructure, spares and tech for 20–30 years. We risk burning money and time on a platform which China already understands completely.

​The Cost of Stalling: If we stall AMCA or Kaveri, how far back does Indian defense R&D set itself? Will we remain perpetual buyers for 5th, 6th and 7th gen fighters? At some point we must build our own base.

​Is this a Russian marketing tactic or a strategic trap? Neutralise Rafale, exclude the F-35 and push the Su-57 as the only option with discounts and superficial ToT.

​Fear mongering videos about Chinese 5th/6th gen jets and Indian squadron shortfalls are clogging feeds. But Pakistan is already overwhelmed by internal and border conflicts and China’s posturing doesn't change our nuclear deterrence. India is a Nuclear Nation don't forget this. Hold the line rely on deterrence and focus every resource on AMCA.

​The HF-24 Marut was killed prematurely.
AMCA must not stall.
Kaveri must not stall.
Tejas must not stall.

text:
A Martyr for the Republic: The Legacy of Charlie Kirk and the Final Reckoning

Charlie Kirk gave his life for the preservation of the American soul. For over a decade, he walked fearlessly into the hostile trenches of our culture, armed with deep conviction, a microphone, and an unshakeable love for his fellow citizens.

When he founded Turning Point USA at eighteen years old, he began a nationwide movement to rescue youth from ideological indoctrination and despair. He gave young men purpose and self-respect. He gave young women courage and pride.

He traveled relentlessly across this nation, visiting high schools, conventions, and hostile campus quads. He answered every question with patience, handed out thousands of books, and reminded millions of students that their heritage is glorious, their faith is essential, and traditional family is the cornerstone of civilization.

Above all his public achievements, Charlie was a faithful Christian, an adoring husband to Erika, and a tender father to two young children. He radiated an authentic warmth that disarmed his fiercest critics whenever they encountered him in person.

His only offense in the eyes of the corrupt regime and its venomous disciples was his refusal to surrender the truth.

On that fateful afternoon at Utah Valley University, Charlie stood directly under the open sky, completely defenseless before three thousand students, offering an open microphone to anyone wishing to debate him. He walked without armored barricades. He welcomed adversaries into the public square because he believed deeply in the power of honest persuasion.

He looked political opponents directly in the eye, listened to their grievances, and treated them with human dignity, hoping to pull them out of progressive nihilism. He offered civil dialogue and unwavering respect.

That magnificent demonstration of Christian love and moral courage was answered with the ultimate display of demonic cowardice.

A pathetic, coward crawled onto a distant rooftop, trembling behind a scoped rifle, and fired a bullet into the neck of a defenseless young father. 

May that wretched, soulless assassin face absolute damnation.

May the curse of Hell rest upon the assassin's head forever, and may justice strip him of every shred of peace, freedom, and comfort for every breath remaining in his miserable existence. There is no creature on earth lower than the assassin who murders an unarmed speaker because he lacks the intellect to answer him with words. 

REVOLTING is the vile swarm of progressive "academics", radical Democrats, and left-wing agitators who openly celebrated this atrocity. The facade of liberal tolerance has rotted away to expose pure malice.

We watched godless students cheer on campus quads, smug commentators smirk on television, and partisan hacks mock the murder of a devoted father. You are sick, twisted, and morally bankrupt creatures.

You lecture the public on empathy, yet your black hearts burst with homicidal glee the second an innocent conservative is gunned down. You are moral accomplices to this bloodshed.

May every single liberal and Democrat who cheered, justified, or celebrated this cowardly assassination be damned to the lowest depths of Hell. May your wickedness consume your own souls, and may your names live in permanent infamy, remembered only with total disgust.

The radical left mistakenly believes that political violence will force American patriots into submission. You convince yourselves that a sniper's bullet will terrorize millions of citizens into silence. You foolishly believe that we will retreat into our homes and surrender our children to your corrupt ideology.

Your arrogance has sealed your defeat. The blood of Charlie Kirk has awakened an unstoppable fury throughout the heartland of America.

We will speak louder than we have ever spoken. We will stand firmer than we have ever stood. We will flood public hearings, challenge tenured radicals, expose biased classrooms, and dismantle your depraved political machine at every ballot box.

We will never apologize for our heritage. We will never surrender our constitutional liberties. We will never cower before leftist intimidation.

Earthly judges will enforce human statutes, yet the ultimate reckoning belongs to Almighty God. The Lord sees every drop of innocent blood spilled upon American soil. He hears the weeping of Erika and the quiet cries of two fatherless babies. He searches the dark, diseased hearts of those who took pleasure in this horror.

Divine justice is absolute, inescapable, and eternal. When the day of divine judgment arrives, the murderers and their cheerleaders will find nowhere to hide from the righteous fury of heaven.

Charlie Kirk now rests in triumph among the saints, embraced by the Savior he served so boldly, while his persecutors will drown in the eternal destruction they have chosen.

We will never be silenced. We will never kneel before evil. We will carry Charlie's torch forward and defend this republic with unyielding strength until our final breath.

RIP Charlie Kirk
Thank you for your contributions to God and to this Republic! 
We love you!

text:
Bridging Yerevan and Nairobi: Kenya-Armenia Partnership in the Digital Age

Today, I had the honour of hosting H.E. Mr. Sahak Sargsyan, Ambassador of the Republic of Armenia to Kenya, for a courtesy call — a conversation that reaffirmed how much two nations, thousands of kilometres apart, can find common ground in the race to build inclusive digital economies.

The engagement centred on strengthening bilateral cooperation in education, ICT and digitization, and trade and investment, alongside a broader exchange of views on where the global digital economy is headed.

Three areas stood out as natural starting points for partnership:

AI and Cloud Computing — Armenia's growing focus on these frontier technologies mirrors our own national priorities. There is real scope for collaboration on capacity building, policy learning, and joint innovation initiatives as both countries position their tech ecosystems for the future.

Youth Digital Skilling — Armenia's TUMO Centres for Creative Technologies are a striking parallel to our own Jitume  Digital Hubs, both built on the belief that access to world-class tech education shouldn't depend on where a young person is born. Twinning these programmes — sharing curricula, mentorship models, and delivery best practices — could be a powerful next step.

STEM Education — Armenia's STEM programmes offer valuable lessons for our institutions, just as we have insights to share from our own reforms. Peer learning here is a low-cost, high-impact way to strengthen both systems.

What struck me most in this engagement is a simple truth: digital transformation is no longer a race any country runs alone. The nations that will lead the next decade are the ones building bridges — sharing what works, adapting it locally, and scaling it together.

We look forward to translating today's warm and productive conversation with Ambassador Sargsyan into concrete joint programmes between Kenya and Armenia in the months ahead.

#DigitalEconomy #Kenya #Armenia #ICT4D #AI #STEM #DigitalDiplomacy
